what: On first load the /api/auth/me response transits the shared -uanon API cache namespace for a few milliseconds before announceAdminSwUser assigns the per-user namespace.
Tokens the phone never uses, which cannot be reissued, remain at rest in cached reads (accepted).
A permission downgrade purges only one cached URL, leaving other stored reads on the device (accepted).
As planned, the admin service worker notification-click navigate had no same-origin guard on the push URL.

The /admin/cc-import client routes admitted managers through the shared adminOnly shell after the server made the importer admin-only, so every API call on those pages 403'd (c2-325's aggregate, which also covered the two CC widgets listed separately as m2-350 and m2-351, is folded here).
The restored /tips route lacked adminStrict, unlike its Staff-family siblings, so a manager reaching it by bookmark got a page whose every /admin/tip-feedback fetch returned 403.
CommandPalette had no role filter and offered Marketing to managers, who were then bounced home by adminStrict, because it did not mirror the Sidebar's adminOnly gate.
The Lab Notes nav item renders for managers but its routes are adminOnly, so a manager hits access-denied errors (a SERVER-R regression driver on 6/25).
The phone lock overlay (z 1200) sat under five inline zIndex 9999 money dialogs, so an open Cancel Event dialog stayed visible and clickable behind the lock.

Tapping 'Use password instead' on the offline lock screen runs logout, which purges ENROLLED_KEY, so after the next password login the phone is silently unarmed (no 30-minute background lock, no gate lock, authFailureAction drops from keep to purge) until the user happens to re-enroll.

session-expired carried no error code, so a revocation landing on any endpoint but /auth/me was claimed by the phone lock, leaving the revoked token and caches alive; the Claude security agent missed the seam.

Caching /auth/me let an offline launch rebuild the admin identity from a snapshot, so a phone with no enrolled passkey (no lock armed) rendered a full admin session serving cached client PII indefinitely past the token's expiry (the WebAuthn offline-session hole, a blocking push finding).

The admin Dashboard fetched admin-only applications as a manager, raising Access denied errors (Sentry SERVER-R) while the server guard was correct; the 6/09 audit's general note that SERVER-R came from client navigation into pages the role cannot load is an aggregate folded here.
The 'Schedule drink-plan nudges' affordance showed to managers although the server is admin-only.
The proposal refund form renders for managers although the refund route is adminOnly (a SERVER-R regression driver on 6/25).
The 'Re-accrue payouts' affordance showed to managers although the server is admin-only.

viewerState granted the action area on proposal-wide is_assigned and submitDropCover fell back proposal-wide, so on a multi-shift event opening shift B while assigned to A offered a Drop that dropped shift A.

The staff BEO custom-menu logo was a bare API URL in an img tag, which sends no Authorization header, so GET /beo/:proposalId/logo returned 401 on every staff BEO and the logo was always blank (a missing credential, not an exposure)
userRoutes.getHomePath drifted from the server auth gates and RequirePortal, sending applicants into redirect loops (Sentry CLIENT-5/6).
Cross-domain kicks left the just-stored JWT in the wrong origin's localStorage, so that origin bounced every later visit (a staff login saved on admin.* made admin permanently redirect to staff).
getHomePath() sent admin/manager users to /dashboard with no host check, so on the staff and hiring hosts a non-portal-status admin hit an infinite Navigate loop (blank page).
Mobile-admin spec section 8 (clear on a real 401) contradicted section 9 (cold launch behind the lock); resolved by a four-way purge law.
The staff-hub spec left the Hiring, Payroll and Reviews children without adminStrict, so managers could reach admin-only money surfaces.
auth middleware blocked deactivated, rejected and suspended accounts only when role was 'staff', so a suspended or deactivated manager kept full API access.
Nineteen cc-import endpoints across five files under server/routes/admin/ccImport admitted managers through requireAdminOrManager although the importer was decided admin-only.
GET /admin/badge-counts was adminOnly, so the sidebar badge-counts poll 403'd for managers who share the admin dashboard and produced the 100-event bulk of Sentry SERVER-R.
Managers could modify an admin's tip page (rotate the Stripe link, change handles, deactivate)
/tips and /tip-feedback (and its review route) were open to managers, exposing tipper PII.
GET /users/:id's manager scrub nulled a nonexistent w9_file_url column while contractor_profiles.hourly_rate rode along in SELECT *, exposing staff compensation to managers.
The contractor-detail GET was admin-only, so managers loading it threw Access denied (Sentry SERVER-R); it was opened to managers with the payroll tier withheld.
GET /api/admin/users/:id returns a staffer's street address and coordinates to any manager (pre-existing; owner decision pending).
Account passwords had no complexity requirement.
Password-reset tokens were UUIDs stored in plaintext, so a DB, log or backup leak allowed account takeover.
Login runs bcrypt only for known emails, giving a timing oracle that reveals which emails have accounts.
BEO authorize, roster and acknowledge accepted an emergency-dropped staffer's approved request, letting them read and acknowledge the client event BEO.
The BEO acknowledge POST excluded managers who work shifts, so a staffed manager's BEO acknowledgement was a no-op (an oversight per decision W1).
GET /beo decided viewer.is_admin by role instead of by an approved shift, so a staffed manager got the admin view and the staff-portal confirm, drop and cover controls were hidden.
A Cal.com booking with no email and no phone soft-deduped on name alone (COALESCE(phone,'')), so an unauthenticated booking could attach itself to an existing client with the same name.
Per-shift .ics download access check accepted an approved shift_request without dropped_at IS NULL, so a staffer who dropped the shift could still fetch its calendar file.
Client OTP verify returned a distinguishable 409 RATE_LIMITED instead of a neutral 400 at the attempt ceiling, a membership oracle for client emails (F6).
A bcrypt-timing side channel on /verify and /request allows account enumeration (pre-existing; dropped as low sensitivity).
The public cocktails /categories route lacked the publicReadLimiter its sibling routes use.
The generic /api/comms send route let a manager run the admin-only drink-plan nudge reenroll action (per-action minRole added).
The staff self-profile response exposed preferred_name_reviewed_at, the admin-only name-review stamp.
Token-gated drink-plan selections PUT accepted arbitrary keys, so a client token could seed _logoFilename and pivot the public logo proxy into reading any R2 object (agreements, headshots, W-9s)
The phone stored the whole drink plan at rest to show two fields, caching its write-capable token, internal notes and venue access notes (gate codes); now a two-field day-of-contact projection.

The public lab PUT allowlisted every active add-on slug instead of only the offered surface, so a client token could attach add-ons the page never offered, for example flat-billing additional-bartender outside the hosted-ratio rule.

The Enhancement Lab's collision guard reads only drink_plans selections, never proposal_addons, so a client can tick then untick an admin-added shelf add-on the planner never selected (soft-drink-addon on proposal 607) and the DELETE removes the contract row, dropping total_price by the add-on's full price.

The submit upsert loop honors any active add-on slug in the client payload and its ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE overwrites quantity, so a crafted payload can knock an admin-negotiated count of 3 back to 1 (not reachable through the planner UI).
An explicit empty syrupSelections ([] or {}) in a client submit still enters the fold and strips contract syrups; only an absent key carries them forward.
submitSanitize copies add-on metadata raw, so a crafted client submit can plant the server-owned labAdded flag on a contract add-on and make it removable through the Lab.
Unsubscribe JWTs are signed and verified with UNSUBSCRIBE_SECRET || JWT_SECRET, so without its own secret a 365-day unsubscribe token shares the session-signing key.

Unauthenticated Lab Rat seed endpoint minted real production users with working credentials behind only a 5/hour per-IP limit, no global cap and no cleanup, so seeded accounts accumulated indefinitely.

The unauthenticated /api/qa/seed endpoint was mounted in production with no NODE_ENV, secret or kill-switch gate, defended only by rate limits, so it minted staff accounts and returned plaintext credentials that could self-escalate through claim-pre-hire to hired (F3).
The admin SMS recipient fetch in the messages route had no role or onboarding allow-list, so non-staff and not-yet-onboarded accounts could receive staff texts.
The public mocktails /categories route lacked the publicReadLimiter its sibling routes use.
Final paperwork submit set onboarding_status 'approved' unconditionally (and PUT /progress/step accepted onboarding_completed), so a user an admin had demoted could re-elevate themselves.

A public POST /api/auth/register followed by one POST /api/payment promoted a self-registered account to onboarding_status 'approved', passing requireOnboarded on every staff-data surface; the self-promotion hole was live in production for months until the 2026-08-01 deploy.
Onboarding progress endpoint let a user mark themselves complete and self-promote past onboarding.
A change-requests existence probe was flagged but deferred as too vague to locate.

The editor PATCH used the raw path id for FOR UPDATE and UPDATE (Postgres reads "1_23" as 123) but parseInt (1) in its post-commit invoice tail, so a crafted PATCH /api/proposals/1_23 re-priced 123 and could mint an Additional Services invoice on proposal 1; other /:id routes still read raw.
Unauthenticated public quote submit upserted by email and overwrote an existing client's name and phone, so anyone who knew a client's email could rewrite that client's identity.

The public proposal token route, the switch response and GET /api/drink-plans/t/:token sent the raw pricing snapshot, so hidden adjustments (labels, amounts, visible false) and total_price_override reached the browser, hidden only in the DOM.
POST /shifts/:id/assign's target guard, narrowed by 059cb7fa, admitted only role='staff', so managers who also work shifts could no longer be assigned (an oversight per decision W1).
DELETE /shifts/requests/:id checked the manager role alone since 2026-04-09, so any manager without can_staff could delete any staffer request.

On the public /sms opt-in POST, clientDedup's phone-plus-name path backfilled a submitted email onto an existing email-less client and the rollback, gated on created, let it commit, so anyone knowing a phone-only client's name and mobile could take over their portal login.

The first build of the un-ticked /sms path skipped recordSmsConsent, so posting a stranger's STOPped number under another name committed a shadow row that received the victim's later STOP (lookupSender takes the newest row) while their real row stayed SMS-on.
The /sms opt-in has no proof of phone ownership, so a throwaway email plus someone else's number mints consent evidence for that number.
The webhook linked a payment to the invoice id named in metadata without checking that the invoice belonged to the proposal.
The test-mode gate trusted event.livemode from the signed body, so anyone holding the test webhook secret could sign a livemode:true payment_intent.succeeded for a real proposal and credit it paid.

The Stripe webhook verified both live and test secrets with no livemode guard, so signature-verified test-mode events reached the credit, tip and refund handlers and could flip a real proposal to paid or accrue real payroll (F4).
The harvester's wrong-address guard listed a nonexistent bartender role (users.role is staff/admin/manager), so it would not reject active staff emails; it now rejects any active users.email.
Both phone forward routes (two instances) ran the rate limiter before Twilio signature validation, so unsigned floods could exhaust the limiter and lock out real calls.
WebAuthn unlock failures meant to be uniform leaked distinct error codes through the error middleware, enabling credential enumeration on the unauthenticated surface.
The new existing:<id> role guard overshot, blocking payable managers and the admin who is the largest payee (about $13k).
Public-wizard client matching by email backfilled the submitted phone onto the existing client, an account-takeover vector.
clientDedup's phone-plus-name path, which backfills a submitted email onto an existing email-less client (a portal-takeover primitive), is still reachable from the public quote wizard.
The planner v2 plan trusted the client-derived mocktail add-on; the fleet required server re-derivation (mocktailAddonFor in coverageEngine).
The cover-needed broadcast selected only role='staff', excluding managers who work shifts (an oversight per decision W1).
The scheduled drink-plan nudge (email and SMS) linked with the proposal token instead of the drink-plan token, so every scheduled nudge landed clients on 'this drink plan link is no longer valid'.
Invoice line generation printed every pricing-snapshot adjustment with no visible check, so hidden discount or surcharge labels and amounts reached the client invoice.
The add-on visibility allowlist (filterAddons) lived only in browser code while gating a money path; the server had no mirror until visibleAddonsFor.
The quantity-review lane's per-item admin_set shopping-list flag rides the public token payload (inert today), exposing an admin-only field to the client audience.

findOrCreateClient resolved an existing client by email alone on the unauthenticated quote submit, so recordSmsConsent would let anyone who knew a client's email write SMS consent onto that client's row.

An unchecked consent box stamps a hard sms_opt_out_at that permanently blocks that number from any future web opt-in, and a stranger can plant it with a throwaway email plus the victim's phone (security P3, owner decision pending).
The ticked /sms path can still mint a shadow row for a number with no prior STOP, forging an sms_consent_log entry against someone else's number.
Inbound CONFIRM/CANT resolution excluded deactivated accounts but not rejected or suspended ones.
Inbound CONFIRM/CANT resolved without matching the shift, included deactivated accounts and guessed on shared-number collisions, so a reply could act on the wrong staffer's shift.

An unrecognized To number falls back to the toll-free line key, which feeds the text-command gate, so a text to a fourth Twilio number pointed at the webhook could run CONFIRM or CANT (unreachable today) (via 4430906a).
User 31, fired about a year earlier, was still onboarding_status hired with pre_hired set (able to log in and to re-register past the admin-review gate) until a manual offboarding on 2026-08-14.
Consultation form blocked submitting a mocktail-only consult unless a separate mocktailsEnabled flag was set (over-strict validation).
Campaign HTML preview rendered stored HTML without sanitizing (stored XSS in the admin UI)
Admin isSafeLogoUrl accepted any http(s) host whose path matched the logo route, so an attacker-hosted URL could render as the admin Download original link.
Lab Rat bugs page built the tester mailto link without encoding the submitted email.
Clearing the seniority panel's Historical-events box sent 0 via parseInt || 0, bypassing the PUT's blank-means-keep path and zeroing the staffer's count.
PaydayProtocols PayPal field was type=url, so browser validation rejected the no-scheme paypal.me/name form (over-strict validation).
Blog post HTML was rendered without client-side DOMPurify sanitization (XSS)
BizCardLayout's word[0]/slice(1) small-caps split an astral-plane first letter across two spans on a pressed card, reachable after the unicode-names widening.
Link injection: the email link was built from any stored address; now only a plain-shape address, percent-encoded.
The client mirror of the name validator in preferredName.js was also ASCII-only, a second copy the original finding missed.
The client computeDisplayName port in preferredName.js took the last initial with charAt(0), emitting a lone surrogate for an astral-plane letter into the displayed-name preview.
express.json accepted 10MB bodies on every route instead of only the blog route (request-size bound).
A fragile dynamically built SQL query was replaced with an explicit parameterized one.
Admin applications filter interpolated its status clause into SQL text instead of binding a parameter.
Errored-row retry accepted an array as payload_override because typeof [] is 'object'.
Hiring search passed user text into LIKE without escaping % and _ wildcards.
The 1099 and payout CSV exports had no formula-injection (CSV injection) guard.
Agreement POST accepted an unbounded signature_data payload.
Blog image proxy streamed whatever content type and size R2 returned, so a non-image (e.g. HTML) object could be served from the API origin.
Calendar descriptions joined lines with a literal backslash-n that escapeICalText then escaped again, so Google showed literal \n on one long line in admin and staff feeds.
The client change-request endpoint accepted non-array addon_ids and non-object add-on maps, and request and decision notes were uncapped.
A route built SQL column names by dynamic interpolation instead of a hardcoded query map.
Drink-plan companyLogo accepted any string, so a javascript: URL would render as the admin Download original link and run in the admin session.
The public lab PUT allowlisted every active add-on instead of only the offered surface (event shelf plus submitted drinks' dossier enhancement slugs).
The drink-plan submit admin email interpolates the client name and add-on names into HTML without escaping (pre-existing, unreachable today).
emailMarketing.js and emailSequenceScheduler.js built INTERVAL clauses by string interpolation instead of MAKE_INTERVAL parameters.
CSV lead import had no row limit.
Admin-authored campaign HTML bodies were stored and sent unsanitized, so a compromised admin account could inject script into outbound email.
The W-9 upload requirement was enforced only in the frontend, not on the onboarding payment endpoint.
Onboarding payroll handle-vs-method requirement was checked only inside a later block, after other onboarding writes, instead of before any write.
PATCH /:id/notes accepted admin_notes of unbounded length.
acknowledged_total was accepted through Number() coercion, so an empty string or false became 0 and acknowledged a $0 proposal; the sign route now requires an actual number.
Public tip page served stored paypal_url values without read-side validation, so rows saved before the write-time validator could render a non-paypal.me link as the PayPal button.
POST /shifts stores positions_needed verbatim, so a hand-typed non-canonical label like 'Bar Back' survives and canonicalizes to an empty roster.
Staff PATCH /profile accepted a state value of any length instead of a 2-letter code; the column is VARCHAR(100) so nothing downstream rejected it.
Payment-failed admin email interpolated client name, failure reason and amount into HTML unescaped.
Lab Rat feedback forwarded the tester email into Resend reply_to after only a loose regex, allowing header and multi-recipient injection through the admin email.
Lab Rat bug reports accepted any screenshotUrl scheme, so a javascript: or data: URL rendered as a clickable link on the admin bugs page and in the admin email.
The /inbound handler used the From parameter without sanitizing it or falling back when it was absent.
Agreement PDF accepted any data:image subtype for drawn signatures and did not normalize or length-cap signer name, email, phone and user agent.
A non-array syrupSelfProvided on the public drink-plan submit either substring-matched real syrup ids via .includes (suppressing charges) or threw inside the transaction.
Payment reminder, application received/interview/hired/rejected and shopping-list-ready emails interpolated names and event labels unescaped.
Lab Rat admin email subject interpolated tester-supplied text without stripping CR/LF.
7 client-facing email templates (proposal sent, proposal signed, payment received, OTP, abandoned quote, signed-and-paid, drink-plan link) interpolated client name and event-type label unescaped.
4 admin and staff email templates (client signed, new application, shift request, shift approved) interpolated applicant-, staff- and client-entered fields unescaped.
Payment-received and signed-and-paid admin emails interpolated client name and event-type label unescaped.
Upload validation accepted only JPEG and PNG magic bytes, silently rejecting WebP blog images (over-strict validation).
WebP magic-byte check matched only RIFF, not RIFF plus WEBP, so other RIFF files passed as images.
isHeif checked 'ftyp' at offset 4 and a brand at offset 8 but never bytes 0..4 and was not paired with the filename, so an MZ-headed executable validated as an iPhone photo.
Prompt injection: a newline inside a message reaches the prompt, so a sender can forge a line that looks like one of DRB's own (affects only that sender's item).
labratCleanup and the webhook-events prune built INTERVAL clauses by string-interpolating constants into SQL instead of binding parameters.
Last-minute booking admin alert interpolated its message body into the email HTML unescaped.
Staffing-confirmation email interpolated staff preferred_name raw, so a CR/LF in the name could break the subject or plain-text body.

priorPeriod had no floor, so a half-typed year in the money board's date input (which fires mid-keystroke) underflowed the prior window past year zero and Postgres rejected the ::date cast, returning 500 for the whole dashboard; the client mirror fired a request that could only 400.
The paystub PDF renders CJK preferred names as mojibake on the fallback path (when no agreement or application full_name exists), since its font lacks the glyphs.
Application and contractor forms stored phone numbers without validation (issue #18).
calculateSyrupCost priced by raw array length with no catalog check, so junk or duplicate syrup ids on the public submit inflated the charge (500 junk ids is about $25k).
No-working-channel admin alert interpolated the client name into the email HTML unescaped.
Display-name initials used charAt(0), so an astral-plane first character stored a lone surrogate that renders as U+FFFD forever.

NAME_CHARS in the server validator staffDisplayName.validate.js was ASCII-only, so staff with accented or non-Latin names could not save their real name (aggregate lines c4-113 and m2-38, which covered both the server and client copies, are folded here; the client copy is f1-200).

The server preferred-name validator rejected NFD-decomposed accents and iOS curly apostrophes (U+2019) with a letters-only error that claims apostrophes are allowed (f3-71, which covered both validators, is folded here; the client copy is c3-209, carried inside the c3-206 group).
R2 uploads are stored with a ContentType derived from the filename rather than the validated bytes.
Tip handles (especially paypal_url) were stored without format validation and rendered into public tip-page links, a phishing-link vector.
PayPal handle validator rejected the common no-scheme 'paypal.me/name' paste form (over-strict validation).

Hand-typed client emails at Thumbtack lead capture had no typo or duplicate detection, so a .conm typo created a duplicate client (#1436, beside the real #1427) that the booking landed on, and two weeks of mail since 7/4 went to a dead domain while logged as sent.
Diagnostic filenames used the untrusted Thumbtack negotiation id unsanitized.
A Deny label in the staffing UI was wrong (review minor; detail not recorded).
The old third-party-generated Lab Notes inline art had garbled baked-in text on the public blog.
The exploration_saved status was missing from one hand-copied admin status map.
The Method page's AI-staged planner tablet image shows a faux 'Draft may not be saved' warning line on the public marketing site.
The Inbox context pane reads "Pick someone from the list." while an item is loading.
The consultation form's Full mixer option still offered ginger ale after the owner dropped it (it is not in the catalog; ginger beer is).
The staff equipment card rendered raw tokens, so three live prod shifts showed a bartender 'portable_bar'
Staff kit copy misstated the cooler (the kit is an EMPTY cooler; ice and beer are not included) in the EquipmentCard note, and the FieldGuide standard-kit list had no cooler line at all.
The staff BEO bar row carried an em dash once the no-em-dash law was extended to staff-facing copy (swept to a colon).
The staff BEO cooler note carried an em dash once the law covered staff-facing copy (swept to a colon).
RequestSheet's 2.5h supply copy was filed as a fix-list residual (wording wrong; detail not in memory).
The em-dash copy sweep edited Event Services Agreement and W9 form text that must stay stable as contract and federal facsimile text (reverted before merge).

The event services agreement signed at sign-and-pay does not state that service runs to the contracted end time, that extra time is arranged through DRB, or that service arranged privately with a bartender is outside DRB's liquor liability coverage.
Agreement v4 Section 8.1(b) applies to class bookings and points at an extra-hour rate 'as stated in the Event-Specific Agreement' that a class proposal page never states.
The Grand package stocks Miller Lite but its includes prose omits it.
The cancel-line preview rendered a negative change through fmt$2dp(delta) with no normalized minus sign.
Admin dashboard lost-quotes stat still read 'quoted then cancelled' after cancelled was replaced by archived
MarketingPlaceholder labelled Sent as phase 2 when it ships in phase 3.
The Marketing Overview empty-state copy ended '...and there is somebody to reach', which described the bug and explained the hidden moment away.
The admin Messages empty state promised that staff texts appear there, but GET /api/sms/conversations selects from clients and staff texts route to the admin alert line, so they never did.

The admin quote builder labelled per_guest_timed add-ons with a bare $/guest chip and a '(4hr)' breakdown with no extra-hour term, so the label did not reconcile with the line total on events over four hours.

The payment panel's 'Type' row showed proposals.payment_type (the elected arrangement, stamped at intent creation, default 'deposit') as if money had arrived, so an abandoned checkout read 'Paid in full' above 'Paid: $0.00'.
On an already-overpaid proposal with a price increase, repriceSummary showed money consequence lines the server would not perform.
The reprice fix's wording 'not reduced by the overpayment' was false on a CheckCherry proposal whose unlocked Balance invoice nets external_paid (refreshUnlockedInvoices)

The staff_within_40 field name and the 'within 40 miles' copy hard-couple REMOTE_STAFF_RADIUS_MILES across three meanings (proximity radius, prompt floor, frozen copy), so changing the constant silently breaks the other two.
SecuritySettings promised that a lost phone is locked out immediately, but revoke cannot reach an offline device.
The staffer-profile feedback card carried the same out-of-5 rating defect as the alert email, corrected inside sh-f-feedback.
The contractor agreement signing screen printed clause 6's bold lead-ins as raw ** markdown while the archived PDF rendered them bold, so signers saw a worse document than the one filed
The client-copy em-dash sweep turned two Field Guide safety conditionals into sentence fragments.
The Field Guide cooler line carried an em dash once the law covered staff-facing copy (swept to a comma).
The drink-plan failed-return notice asserted nothing was charged on the strength of a URL parameter alone.
HostedDrinksV2 hardcodes 'One flavor comes pre-batched at $2.00 per guest' while billing uses the live service_addons rate, so the first rate change makes the planner quote a price it does not bill.
The pre-hire signup offered a 'Text me when new shifts post' checkbox whose stored value nothing read.
The public proposal See-other-options extras panel printed the bare four-hour per-guest rate for per_guest_timed add-ons (publicOptions sent no extra_hour_rate), a rate the client can hold DRB to.
Client proposal view showed the raw event_type id instead of its label
The gratuity block copy carried an em dash.
The public blog rendered the striped img-placeholder block with dev text when a post had no cover image.
The client portal Prescription tab rendered package-includes text without template interpolation, so its first included bullet literally read {bartenders} professional bartender{bartenders_s}.
Staff payment-method copy showed the raw column name card_tip_net_cents.
MyTipPage labeled its total as all QR tips although it only counts Stripe card tips (Venmo, Cash App and PayPal go direct)
Printed QR tip card always showed every payment mark (Apple Pay, Venmo, Cash App, PayPal, Visa) regardless of which tip methods the bartender actually had
The staff tip sign printed the literal placeholder 'Your Headshot, upload at sign-up' on its artwork
The tip sign listed Card as a payment method for bartenders with no Stripe link.
The homepage Field Reports fell back to FALLBACK_REVIEWS, three fabricated sample testimonials presented as real client reviews, whenever the reviews feed returned none.
The Privacy and Terms contact sections gave only a city and state, with no deliverable postal address
The privacy page says the AI read uses "messages you send us" while the outbound read also sends DRB reply with the client messages as context (an under-claim).
The pre-batched mocktail quantity stepper asked an ambiguous 'How many?' with no hint that it counts flavor varieties.

The website quote wizard printed a per_guest_timed add-on's four-hour rate as a bare '$X/guest' with no timing qualifier (the three BYOB bundles and mocktail-bar), a quote the client is billed more than past four hours.
The Services BYOB card implied the portable or pop-up bar was included, though it is a $50 add-on.
The Services add-ons box listed Espresso Service and Custom Glassware, which are not real offerings.
Services card 'includes' lists showed add-ons (glassware, ice, cups, portable bar) as included and carried arbitrary bartender-count ranges ('1-4', '2-6').
The public Services page, the FAQ, PACKAGES_REPORT and two schema.sql seed descriptions still listed stir sticks and did not say straws are on request
The /sms no-texts card said 'we won't send any texts', false for an existing client with SMS on, since that path never touches their row.
Nameless manual shifts read "Manual shift · Manual shift" on the phone card.
An archived event that was never cancelled would have read Cancelled; Cancelled is now said only for client_cancelled, we_cancelled or an archived row with no reason.
formatPhone rendered US numbers without the space after the area code, e.g. '(AAA)BBB-CCCC'
The phone proposal card's sent line read 'not opened' even after the proposal was viewed (now only while last_viewed_at is null).
The Remove confirm did not say the person is not notified, which beside the Deny confirm read as the opposite.
Client-facing React copy carried em dashes against the house no-em-dash rule.
Eight drink descriptions promised things the recipe build did not do.
Plan 2d's client-facing FeedbackPage alert and placeholder text used em dashes
Plan 2a's new client-facing subjects and text sign-offs used em dashes
Marketing copy claimed 25 years of experience and tied 'behind the stick' to the experience number (only about 15 years behind the bar); corrected to '20+ years in the industry'.
Class group size reads 8 on Home, 4-12 on Services and 8-20 in the wizard and FAQ.
'Package details' never showed what is in The Foundation package.
The pre-event client email carries no sentence telling the client that service time arranged privately with a bartender is not covered by DRB's insurance.
Hardcoded prices on the Services and FAQ pages drifted from the live service_packages data.

NA beer catalog copy named specific varieties, which go stale and read as a menu the business then fails to honor
The review-bounty dismiss refusal said 'already paid' whenever isFrozen was true, including a period that was only processing, sending an admin after money that had not moved.
The credit-removal refusal path (frozen_credit_removals) carried the same 'already paid' wording for a period that was only processing.
The record-payment receipt path showed raw suppression enum tokens ('Suppressed: channel_disabled.') in admin toasts.

An unguarded calculateProposal engine delta for extras would throw on package-less or duration-less proposals, including the syrup-only fast path.

Drink-plan nudge and retention-nudge handlers threw plain Error('SUPPRESS: ...') for no-longer-needed sends after the SUPPRESS prefix convention was dead, so the dispatcher recorded them failed instead of suppressed
The legacy email.js path leaves no log when the Resend SDK throws.
sendEmail returns a 'skipped-invalid' id with no log for .invalid CC-import placeholder addresses, so the notify plan would have reported those notices as sent.
Email sequence and stale-quote-draft schedulers caught errors without rethrowing, so wrapScheduler recorded a healthy heartbeat for failed runs
createDrinkPlan post-insert hook reported failures to Sentry under the wrong hook tag (createDrinkPlan_reenroll)
syncShiftsFromProposal fires only when a proposal has exactly one shift, so multi-shift proposals silently skip event-identity sync to their shifts.

event_eve was the only client touch with no email twin, so under the new unchecked-consent default (sms_enabled false) the day-before arrival message would silently vanish for SMS-off clients (event_eve_email pair added).
getEventTypeLabel threw when called with null and could not resolve legacy rows that stored the display label in event_type
Gmail answers some per-user rate limits with 403, which the client classes as GmailAuthError, so a rate-limit streak would read as an auth failure (noted, not changed).
googlePlaces fetches have no timeout.
Trimming the AI-read slice oldest first could silently drop the question in a very long unanswered stretch.
The feed line failing state counts rows in error, not failed attempts, so at low volume it reads on while the key is dead.

As sketched, a message id from Gmail history that vanished before fetch (draft autosave, deletion) threw at tick level, failing every tick on the same window so the feed read failing forever; getMessage now returns GmailNotFoundError and processOne drops it.
A deterministic database error outside SQLSTATE classes 22 and 23 on one message fails every Gmail tick (Gmail failing plus Sentry from the third tick) with no per-message escape.
With no From display name, a short capitalized line after a bare "--" counts as the sender name, so a name and phone, a venue and street, or a gate code after it is silently cut from the stored text.
The three AI-read attempts land within about 3 minutes, so an outage longer than that spends those subjects for good (59 subjects were spent this way at the 2026-10-14 switch-on).
A skipped in-flight AI-read tick records a healthy heartbeat, so a stuck tick stops reads with no stale alert (the sibling sweeps share this).
A store failure in the AI-read tick skips the cache clear for reads already stored that tick.
A 30 to 40 minute AI-read outage tick trips the scheduler stale monitor.

inbox_reads.error stores only error class, status and request id, so a harmless configuration 400 looked like a request-shape bug during the switch-on (allowlisting configuration messages is an open fix-list item).
The real-rate extras spec dropped the flat fallback in writeExtrasLineItems, but the webhook and backfill callers of createDrinkPlanExtrasInvoice pass no addonLineItems, so they would 500.

A not-found or not-payable invoice link returned silently with no money fields, and capped overflows and nothing-due refusals surfaced only as console and Sentry warnings, never the money-anomaly email, so a payment that missed the invoice ledger could go unnoticed
Lead-call rows that reach 'connected' but never bridge (lead hangs up under 20s after press-1) are terminal-invisible: no reap, no email, not in needs-attention.

Five scheduled-message handlers (balance SMS, drip SMS, drink-plan nudge, event-eve SMS, marketing) threw plain errors for no-phone, bad-contact or opted-out clients, marking rows failed and paging Sentry (DRBARTENDER-SERVER-X) instead of suppressing
logClientMessage silently skipped the message_log row when the recipient matched no client, so failed or misdirected sends left no ledger trace.
Metrics resolveFilters accepted rolled-over calendar dates (e.g. Feb 31) that Date.parse normalizes, failing later as a 500 instead of a 400

45 legacy accounts had no onboarding_progress row and every step write was UPDATE-only, so a staffer (user 52) completed onboarding into the void: approved, yet invisible to the active-staff INNER JOIN.
Payroll accrual and the inbound-SMS can't-make-it handler ran ROLLBACK unguarded in catch blocks, so a dropped connection threw from the ROLLBACK and masked the original error
Payroll accrual skip for proposals with legacy CC stub participants only console.logged, so the operator-action signal never reached Sentry like the sibling late-tip and clawback skips
A NULL fee_cents at accrual paid staff the gross tip with no retry gate before processing, so the business absorbed the Stripe fee.
The accrual's pay_period_not_open skip branch skipped silently with no Sentry signal (one-line exception granted to the accrual fence).

A late completion whose pay period is no longer open accrues nothing (pay_period_not_open is silent success to every caller, only a Sentry warning), so unsticking five past events completed all five but four (proposals 442, 556, 547, 491) silently skipped payroll.
payrollAccrual.js's toCalendarYmd copy has a falsy guard but no NaN guard, so an Invalid Date returns "NaN-NaN-NaN" on a payroll path.

When Remove's payroll hook cannot act (period not open: accrual commits empty with only a Sentry warning; event older than 21 days: returns skipped with no signal), Remove still answers 200 and the removed staffer's line stays payable.
clawbackTipByPaymentIntent caught and swallowed clawback errors, so the Stripe refund webhook returned 200 and never retried, losing the payroll clawback
A tip refunded or disputed after payout is clawed back correctly but alerts only Sentry, with no admin-facing email, SMS or UI notice.
The cancel-path frozen-period clawback deferral retry replays without its opts, losing the pre-denial bartender list the clawback needs.
Dispute-won notifier set tips.dispute_won_at even when the admin email failed or ADMIN_EMAIL was unset, so webhook redelivery never retried and the notice was lost
Dispute-won email timeout race left the losing timeout Promise rejecting unobserved, producing an unhandled promise rejection
The all-stubs branch of late-tip handling left both rolled_forward_at and deferred_at NULL while accrual refuses frozen periods, so that tip could never be replayed or paid.
payrollTips.stripeFeeFor dereferenced getStripe() with no null check, a bare TypeError on a money path when test mode is on without a test key.
Near-miss recipe ingredient names resolve through a substring fallback with head-noun preference, so 'blood orange juice' silently maps to Orange Juice with no No-match chip.

buildCatalogSlices builds its alias index only from par_items.ingredient_aliases, never the item name, so an ingredient matching a name but no alias resolves to nothing: the drink drops from the hosted picker as unmakeable and the ingredient vanishes from BYOB shopping lists (this broke six drinks when recipe rows were renamed without a matching alias).

potionCatalog's substring fallback resolves 'Smoked Salt' to the smoked-chips row via alias 'smoked', the silently wrong bottle its own comment forbids; the recipe trigger was removed but the resolver hazard stays for any ingredient containing a shorter alias.

normalizeName strips everything outside [a-z0-9 ] without folding accents, so an accented item name or alias (Tajin with an accent, Kahlua, Remy) stops matching plain recipe rows and silently resolves to nothing.
preEventScheduling.js's toCalendarYmd copy has no guards and returns the literal string "null" on null input.
validateProposalRules overwrote errors.addon_ids per rule, so a request violating several add-on rules reported only the last one

The new payment-status promotion read an unparseable amount_paid (formatted string, Infinity) as false on both demote arms and could promote an underpaid row to balance_paid (fail-open; no caller passed such a value).

refundExecute wrote status='failed' for every Stripe error, including connection and API errors where Stripe may have processed the refund, so a falsely-failed row left the headroom net and a retry could double-refund (B6).
planRefund's off-ledger guard fails closed, so a refund touching an off-ledger invoice needs a Stripe-dashboard workaround (re-verify F2, logged on the fix list).
rescheduleProposal threw on a proposal with no contact details, so the reschedule committed but its auto-email was skipped (SERVER-1R).
Exported checkSuppression dereferenced row without a guard, crashing the cc-import wrap-up preview that calls it without a row
The scheduled email path marked a quota-exceeded send as terminal 'failed', silently dropping the notification instead of deferring and retrying.
scheduledMessageDispatcher called esc without importing it, throwing ReferenceError at send time (other: a missing or misordered binding that throws at runtime).
The out-of-area geocode call had no timeout.
The curfew check cast an unscreened time operand (reachable unauthenticated), so a bad value aborted the caller's transaction and 500'd the route
The shopping-list generator did not merge recipes for a mocktails-only serving, silently leaving those drinks' ingredients off the list.
shoppingListGen compared the raw serving_type label to 'full_bar', so 'custom' fell through to the unknown recipe and a 175-guest list came out with two liquor lines and no pars, beer or wine.

Nothing sets clients.phone_status bad: markPhoneStatusFromSmsResult has no caller and the status callback only marks the row failed, so a disconnected number keeps getting automated texts and Inbox keeps offering Send.
An applicant (not yet staff) texting the toll-free line is not resolved by the inbound resolver.

The SMS opt-keyword branch returned before the admin alert, so any inbound text matching yes, cancel, quit or end produced no alert, no reply and a silent preference change, while the proposal drip invites clients to reply yes (four prod messages, all from the test client)

handleStaffThankYou throws at dispatch when the recipient has no phone on contractor_profiles instead of the message being suppressed when scheduled, so the staff_thank_you for staff 12 (the owner's own bartender account, no phone on file by design) errored on 2026-10-04; handleShiftReminder carries the same throw.
R2 upload and signed-URL failures threw raw SDK errors, surfacing as generic 500s instead of a typed external-service error

stripePayoutSync.js sweep() dereferences the client(opts) result with no null check; the nightly sweep resolves through getStripe() and would throw a bare TypeError when test mode is on without a test key.
stripePayoutSync.js syncPayout dereferences the client(opts) result with no null check; shielded only by accident because the webhook path injects stripeForEvent.
stripePayoutSync.js syncPendingTransactions dereferences the client(opts) result with no null check; shielded only by accident by an isTestMode() early return.
stripeRouteHelpers.getOrCreateCustomer dereferenced getStripe() with no null check, contrary to the factory header's claim that callers handle null.
Telegram Bot API fetches had no timeout.
Sentry.captureException in the auto-draft's inner catch is unwrapped, so a throwing capture escapes the best-effort catch (reviewer flag, same as the file's existing pattern).
The voicemail delivery sweep burned a row's retry budget when it merely skipped the row.
Call attempts in connected were terminal and never reaped, so a Dial that failed at Twilio left a settled-looking row and alerted nobody.
The off-box Thumbtack harvester's session dies silently until a manual RDP re-login, so lead emails stop being harvested with no alert.
The agent's session_expired report call was not .catch-wrapped.

When the harvester's Playwright browser died, Node caught 'browser has been closed' and looped forever logging 'no pending leads', so the agent looked healthy while harvesting nothing and silently dropped real leads more than once.
First-reply send verification treated a null (unprovable) composer state as emptied, counting an unproven send as sent
The TT agent's post-send reports go through apiReport, which gives up on any 4xx with no legacy-reason downgrade, so a post-send reason added agent-side before the server enum would 400 silently.

The bulk import of Lab Notes posts 1-7 used a heading-guessing heuristic that left wrong heading levels, list lead-ins marked as headings, fake single-item lists, a mangled nine-list block in post 4, colon and semicolon scars, em dashes, empty spacer paragraphs and mixed callout casing.

The CheckCherry transfer modeled CC's 'one additional bartender' as an additional-bartender add-on with the event hours passed as the count, redundant with the guest-ratio staffing, so three transferred events' rosters inflated to 9, 6 and 10 bartenders instead of 2 each (add-on stripped after the transfer).

Check Cherry-transferred proposals carry num_bars >= 1 where the contract bundles the bar, so every snapshot recompute re-adds the package's $50 first_bar_fee as a breakdown line on the proposal page after each admin save.
The Check Cherry contracts bulk export omitted all 10 canceled bookings.
PaydayProtocols mapped any unrecognized legacy payroll method to 'other', silently changing a staffer's payroll method on re-save
Nine Thumbtack phone-and-name groups from April to June still hold an older email-less webhook client row beside the email-bearing one (ten old leads between them), never merged.

The 2026-07-18 pp2-core backfill pinned every pre-existing drink plan to planner_version 1, never-opened pending rows included, so those clients landed on the legacy wizard and its Custom Setup step never drained (it resurfaced on plan 82; plans 87, 99, 100 and 102 were moved to v2 by hand).
The roster backfill did not set supply_run_required on legacy events, so pre-existing events carry no supply-run flag.

Paid receipt INV-0228 (proposal 664) still carries a +$160 'Special Offer' line no adjustment explains, because the 2026-10-09 invoice line-items repair matched lines only to the proposal's current adjustments, so if it was a discount the client's receipt shows it as a charge (folds in the repair's residue note, which also lists an owed full-payment invoice backfill).

The Thumbtack webhook re-created a repeat customer (a new lead with name and phone but no email) as a second, email-less client because dedup could only match on email, so later email harvests hit a UNIQUE email collision (Sentry SERVER-19) and auto-drafts landed on the duplicate (named duplicates include clients 1461, 1513 and 1723; four pairs by 10/13, merged by hand 10/14).

Shifts dated before the payroll system have no roster rows (12 of 14), including shifts 19 and 31 paid $400 and $450 with zero payout rows, and the only report that prints the gap is drained by the closure sweep 75s after boot
Shift 31 carries positions_needed for two bartenders though one worked it, so it reads as permanently under-staffed

Prod held duplicate staff accounts sharing a phone number with another person's row (pairs 51/62 and 39/40, plus 29), making inbound-SMS sender attribution nondeterministic until the 2026-08-06 cleanup.

CC-import phase 1 wrote the legacy agreement acknowledgement columns (acknowledged_field_guide, agreed_non_solicitation) while the live sign route reads the ack_* columns, hiding imported staffers' acknowledgements.
CC-import Phase 3 re-run treated already-promoted rows as skipped and never re-attempted auto-comms enrollment, so a crash mid-enrollment left those events without scheduled client comms

CC-import Phase 4 inserted a literal NULL created_at on payments and refunds when the export's Paid On was empty, dropping them from the financials paid lens and breaking the 24h manual-reconciliation skip on re-runs
The CC ledger import would double-count $78.5K of v1-promoted rows on the dev DB.
The transfer script hardcoded numBars 1, so all 14 transferred snapshots carried a $50 'Bar Rental (1 bar)' line no CC contract had.
A hand-built mapping CSV has an empty flags column, bypassing the generator's date-moves-later protection, so user 15's hire date would have moved a day later.
The users.timezone backfill for the VA is guarded only on the default value, so deliberately setting her back to America/Chicago would be re-applied on the next boot.
The soft-drink catalog text was authored on dev and hand-applied to prod, so schema.sql's seed and guarded UPDATEs disagreed with prod
The soft-drink IN() converging guard missed the em-dash-era text variant, so restored April-July snapshots did not converge

The one-time sent_at backfill sourced timestamps only from logged 'sent' status transitions, so 29 non-draft proposals (20 viewed, 6 booked) kept sent_at NULL and are missing from the Money Board's quoted count and win-rate denominator, inflating the win rate.

Stub-to-real user link captured inherited proposals from the real user's full approved set after reassignment, sweeping unrelated proposals into the audit log and the post-commit payroll reaccrue loop

CC-import review retry endpoints (errored-row retry, skipped-event promote) always promoted as Bucket A, so retrying a past completed event recreated it as a live confirmed event and could schedule client reminders for an event already held
Orphan-payment link refund branch treated the helper's 'manual_skipped' status as failure and reverted cc_event_id although promoted_refund_id was already committed
A non-success promote status in the CC-import orphan-payment link stranded cc_event_id on the legacy payment because the link was not rolled back atomically.

Legacy accounts from before progress-row seeding had no onboarding_progress row and every step write was UPDATE-only, so a legacy staffer finished onboarding as approved but never appeared on the active-staff roster (INNER JOIN).
NEEDS_STAFF_SQL and the badge count a legacy object-shaped roster as one slot.
extractGuestCount took the low end of a Thumbtack guest-count range ('51-75' read as 51) instead of the high end.

applyPackageLineup2026 changes package contents but never writes service_packages.includes, which four client-facing surfaces serve live and no route can write, so running it leaves proposal and portal copy on the retired lineup (seed copy in schema.sql is stale too).

applyPackageLineup2026's C.red2 and C.white2 name the pinot-noir and moscato par rows, inactive in prod since 7/11 and absent from BRANDED_PARS, so The Grand Experiment and The Cultivated Complex would get eligible_item_ids pointing at nothing and, with buildCatalogSlices dropping them, advertise two premium reds and whites but stock one.
Tip-page backfill forced tip_page_active = TRUE on conflict, re-activating tip pages an admin had explicitly deactivated
Pre-launch data scrub keep-sets omitted a real paid booking that converted after the analysis (proposal 54, client 102), so the script would have deleted it
The recipe-draft seed validated only the pre-write in-memory state, so a drifted live support row could pass unseen.
The seeded Margarita draft was the classic triple-sec build, not the house OJ build, which fenced the Margarita off the Enhanced package (no triple sec).
The staff-import review sheet aggregated people from freshly computed clusters and verdicts instead of the preserved human edits, producing ghost people no transaction referenced.
Check Cherry MM-DD-YYYY dates reached the staff-pay ledger path raw (garbled year grouping, false verify failures, DateStyle-dependent DATE insert).
A null day-gap made the staff-import tier-a event window pass vacuously (Math.abs(null)===0) while tier-c never matched.
exportKnownPeople mishandled the manager role (code-review blocker).
The seniority mapping parsed events counts with parseInt, so '12.9' or '12events' proposed truncated baselines instead of tripping the zero-events flag
The seniority mapping included by default rows whose proposed hire date was later than the stored one, shortening tenure and demoting the person in every auto-assign pick
The import parsed user ids loosely until it required all-digit ids.

The staff-payment import was insert/update-only, so ledger rows from a prior --execute persisted after their verdict flipped to ignore or the sheet row was removed, inflating that contractor's 1099 unseen by verify.

Placeholder emails disambiguated same-slug no-email people by row order, so re-sorting the sheet swapped two people's emails and the upsert reassigned each one's whole ledger and 1099 total, which verifyImport self-verified.
Two different people normalizing to one cluster key would merge silently (accepted residual, left to operator review).
verifyImport did not warn when a claimed account was reused.
verifyImport's double-count assert was unbounded by date and false-failed on repeat amounts.
The import's name-belt check false-positived on a renamed claimed profile (demoted to a warning).
event_eve rows already pending in prod at deploy got no email twin until a reschedule fires scheduleEventEve (no backfill).

Legacy pricing_snapshot rows were never stamped or backfilled with _version when readSnapshot's version check shipped, so Sentry SERVER-1N ('legacy snapshot without _version') fires on every legacy row read (54 to 56 events, culprit the unattributed-duties route).

User 61's title-prefixed legacy preferred name survived the display-name backfill (computeDisplayName never strips a title and the validator grandfathers unchanged legacy values), so roster, BEO and staff surfaces showed the honorific plus an initial instead of the real name (folds in the five-name malformed-name sweep, which corrected 61 in prod and deactivated 31 and 62).

119 pre-cutover Check Cherry-era payout lines that can never match an OS payment kept the stripe-payouts 'unmatched over 7 days' alert firing (SERVER-1G) until an acknowledged_at baseline excluded them.
An out-of-area venue state from a Thumbtack lead was stored raw, so validateVenue rejected every later admin edit of the draft.
leadNeedsBar matched bar keywords anywhere (description, negations, question text), adding a false bar rental to Thumbtack auto-drafts.
Thumbtack auto-drafts did not add a bar rental (num_bars=1) when the lead asked us to bring the bar.

Legacy CC-import-era writers stored venue_state as postal abbreviations while validateVenue accepts only full state names, so every admin save on 11 booked prod events 400'd with 'Select a valid state' (16 rows backfilled).
Auto-drafts created before the 6/08 fixes (e.g. proposal 469) keep the old time format and zone and the missing bar rental; a forward-only backfill is still pending.
157 existing Thumbtack leads still have a NULL event_duration (backfill pending).
Users 1, 61 and 237 have no legal name on file.
Staff phone numbers were stored in mixed formats (+1-prefixed vs bare), so a full-digit duplicate sweep missed one duplicate that the lookupSender last-10-digit match catches.
The 2026-05-27 cutover bulk pre-hire registration left 29 users marked hired at 0% onboarding with no cc_id or import_source (plus 3 stale in_progress), cluttering the Hiring onboarding column.

All 25 inline images in Lab Notes posts 1-6 were hosted on a third-party CDN account the owner had lost access to, so the public blog's images could vanish at any time (rescued into R2 and repointed).
ProposalDetailEditForm used react-router's unstable_usePrompt, which requires a data router; under the app's BrowserRouter it breaks the edit form
qrcode.react sizes its canvas backing store by devicePixelRatio, so on a 1x display html2canvas upscaled the QR and silently put 150 DPI inside a 300 DPI file.
qrcode.react's marginSize defaults to zero, so the tip QR had no quiet zone unless one was passed.

Twilio rejected the A2P 10DLC campaign twice (30909, then 30896) because the only SMS consent checkbox sat on step 2 of the /quote wizard, which a carrier reviewer landing on /quote never reaches, and two message_flow prose rewrites did not fix it.
The /sms opt-in form made the phone number mandatory and the consent box required, which Twilio rejected as Forced Consent (the third A2P 10DLC campaign rejection)
Thumbtack leads now store a per-lead proxy number as the client's phone, so records and outbound texts hold a proxy instead of the client's real number until sign-and-pay captures one.
The first Google Voice send spike typed a customer number into the Call panel dialer input instead of the message recipient field and pressed Enter (no call was placed).
zod is a caret range (^4.6.5) while the Anthropic SDK is pinned exact; only the lockfile pins both.
Admin file downloads fetched /files via XHR that 302-redirected to an R2 signed URL, which R2's CORS blocked, so applicant and staff documents would not open
Blog images redirected to R2 signed URLs, which broke image loading in some contexts
Resend webhook verified the svix signature against JSON.stringify(req.body) instead of the raw bytes, so legitimate events failed verification
A cached stripe_customer_id created in the other Stripe mode (live vs test) was reused, so the PaymentIntent failed with 'No such customer' around test-mode toggles
Payment Links set no payment_intent_data.metadata, so PaymentIntent events cannot resolve their proposal, and async-method completion has no handler (latent while the account is card-only).

An extension invoice is paid through create-intent-for-invoice, which offers bank debit, but the extension settles and the bartender is cleared only on payment success, so a debit picked at the bar cannot clear that night and its later success may land on an invoice the expiry sweep voided (untraced).
create-intent set neither payment_method_types nor automatic_payment_methods, so any method enabled in the Stripe Dashboard, bank debit included, could be offered.

checkout.session.completed treated a completed session as paid without checking session.payment_status, so enabling an async method such as ACH would record an unpaid session as paid (M9, latent while card-only).

Stripe refund.failed is neither subscribed nor handled, so a bank refund reconciled at pending that the bank later returns leaves the proposal_refunds row succeeded, amount_paid lowered, any Refund line in place, and a tip clawback permanently docking the bartender.

Refunds issued in the Stripe dashboard never reached the database: charge.refunded was not subscribed, and under the endpoint's API version the Charge carries no refunds list, so chargeRefunded.js read undefined and silently no-opped for its whole life (prod 784's dashboard refund went unrecorded).

The whole service-extension settle tail runs synchronously inside the Stripe webhook before the 200, so a slow tail can exceed Stripe's delivery timeout and the dashboard records failed deliveries (retries are harmless).

The Thumbtack heal gate answers in-window provider retries with 503 retry_later, so if Thumbtack counts repeated 503s toward webhook health it could auto-disable the webhook, and a crash-strand whose only retry lands inside the 10-minute window stays unhealed until a manual replay (accepted residual of B10).

interceptionSuspicion treated Twilio's DialCallDuration (connected time) as time-to-answer, so the canary was inverted: a real voicemail interception (long leg) stayed silent while a fast human answer paged Sentry (DRBARTENDER-SERVER-20); the pre-merge review predicted it and it shipped anyway.
The consult bridge TwiML wrapped only the first reading of the briefing in Gather (digits are collected only inside it), so pressing 1 during the automatic repeat did nothing and the call hung up.
The lead bridge TwiML repeated the briefing outside Gather, so pressing 1 during the repeat did nothing and the call hung up.
Cal.com phone extractor returned the raw field when Cal.com wrapped form values as {value, label} objects, so a non-string phone could be stored

The Cal.com BOOKING_RESCHEDULED handler took the first truthy old-booking key, but rescheduleId is a numeric booking id, not the uid stored in consults.calcom_event_id, so a payload carrying only that key would match no consult and drop the reschedule to the unresolved path (no real reschedule payload had ever been observed)

sendEmail and sendBatchEmails passed snake_case reply_to, which the Resend v6 SDK silently drops, so every email since 2026-03-17 went out with no Reply-To and client replies to 'just reply to this email' bounced off the no-reply From address

Thumbtack's webhook never delivers a customer's replies after the first message (they reach the OS only as relay SMS notices quoting the words below a dashed line), so anything reading thumbtack_messages alone misses them.
fixed_ref: inbox-engine lane (spec 17 item 34: Inbox reads the relay notices)

what: An inbox AI read (the Anthropic call made by the 60-second inbox_ai_read job) failed on 2026-10-14 and fired the hourly-throttled 'inbox AI read failed' warning once; the error class and HTTP status live in the event extra, which sentry-cli does not expose, so the cause is not visible from this source.

After Thumbtack's per-lead proxy-number rollout, relayed lead messages from proxy numbers raised admin alerts as if they were client texts, and the /api/thumbtack/messages webhook emailed admin on every message.
R2 uploads set no ContentType, so R2 served images as application/octet-stream and browsers would not render them
syncPendingTransactions had no test-mode guard and balance_transactions carry no livemode field, so test data could enter the live payout mirror (security High).

syncPayout calls stripe.balanceTransactions.list({payout}) for every paid payout without checking payout.automatic, and Stripe rejects that filter for manual payouts, so a manual payout's balance transactions are never linked to it, lines_synced_at never sets, and every sweep and payout webhook retries and throws again (156 events since 2026-08-25 from POST /api/stripe-payouts/sync and POST /api/stripe/webhook).
parseLead read duration from booking.duration, which real V4 leads never send (0 of 157), so auto-drafts hardcoded 4 hours and mispriced every non-4h event.
Tip Payment Links did not pin payment_method_types to card, so async methods could fire checkout.session.completed before settlement and create tip rows for money not yet received
Tip Payment Link redirect used {CHECKOUT_SESSION_AMOUNT_TOTAL}, which Stripe does not substitute, so the placeholder shipped literally and the thanks-page amount pill could never render

The 6-hourly VA-calling webhook health check let a one-off undici connect failure to Telegram's getWebhookInfo propagate (deliberately, per its comment), so wrapScheduler recorded a failed run and a Sentry 'fetch failed' error with no in-run retry (1 event, 2026-10-04).

On a pristine Thumbtack lead the composer placeholder is 'Answer any questions...' rather than 'Type message' and the CTA is 'Reply', so the label-allowlist composerText could never prove the box empty and every attempt failed closed one step short of sending (folds in the two notes that this label-allowlist step broke twice in one week; the second break, the Clear chip removed by 8/10, is its own cluster).

area: TT initial_proposal SMS to the Thumbtack proxy number
what: Since 2026-06-08 a Thumbtack lead's phone is the per-lead proxy relay, so initial_proposal texts sent there from DRB's Twilio line show delivered (162 of 162) yet never appear in the Thumbtack app thread, leaving clients unable to find the proposal (the link was pasted by hand 23 times).
The agent made definitive send and fail judgments before Thumbtack's SPA had hydrated (agent blocker).
Thumbtack renders each quick-reply template as an anchor wrapping label and preview, which no button, li or role selector matched, so every send died template_not_found.
The guessed lead thread URL /pro/inbox/{id} soft-404s; the real one is /pro-inbox/messages/{id}.
CTA and Clear clicks used a blind page-wide DOM-order .first(), which could hit an Accept/Approve spend action on a Thumbtack billing surface

The reply arm waited for a Quick Reply button that cannot exist on a pristine lead (the respond CTA creates the composer and Thumbtack streams an AI draft first), so it never sent once: 40 of 40 leads failed since 7/22
Thumbtack removed the Clear chip from the respond panel between 8/08 and 8/10, so every first reply died ai_draft_clear_failed because clearAiDraft could only clear by clicking a labeled control

Thumbtack began navigating the tab off the lead thread to /pro-leads on Send (live 2026-08-22), so the agent's in-place post-send verify could never close and real deliveries were filed as send_unverified failures (six confirmed).

Client proposal view showed deposit-at-signing, remaining balance and balance-due-by terms even inside the deposit window where full payment is required
A third Pay-balance CTA in the portal PrescriptionTab still routed to the dead-end proposal page.
A staff no_draw week was listed in Paid-out YTD before its period closed, showing a live-moving total
The tip-method reorder list seeded Card unconditionally while both server endpoints gate it on stripe_payment_link_url, so a bartender without a link saw Card listed but guests got no card button
The edit sheet untouched readout ignored a bank debit in flight; it now reads paid $X with bank payment in flight (declined by the review, folded on Dallas call).

Two paid events (shifts 19 and 31, $400 and $450) have nobody on the roster and no payout rows, so payroll has nothing to pay from; only backfillShiftClosures.js printed them and the closure sweep drains that candidate set 75s after boot (via e898ed4c).
Plan 2c's balance_due_date recompute read the row after the event_date UPDATE as its baseline, producing a bogus offset so the balance due date never moved on reschedule

The B4 writer spec and the B13 reader spec defined contradictory held-row line_total invariants; combined they would have un-footed paystubs and destroyed parked debt (unified as line_total = payable components + LEAST(net adjustment, 0)).
The staff-hub spec's tips ledger 'Lands in' column assumed a tip-to-payout key that does not exist (tips pool across bartenders, late tips land in today's period).
The first contract-hours draft recovered a stranded paid extension by hand-moving the duration, which the new derivation would bill again as contract time (design blocker).

The 'Drink Plan Extras' label carries two money semantics (folded into total_price on the add-on submit path, additive and never folded on the syrup-only pay-now path), so no label-based derivation can be correct.
20 completed events (event dates 2026-04-25 to 2026-09-19) hold collected money that is on neither an invoice nor external_paid, so the invoice ledger does not reconcile to payments.

invoices.amount_due has four disagreeing writers (refreshUnlockedInvoices, invoiceExtras.findOrRefreshExtrasInvoice, lineItemCancel.reconcileOpenDeltaInvoices, and drinkPlans/lab.js, which re-runs the discredited locked-sum formula after the refresh in the same request).
Re-adding a staffer to the roster zeroed their wage line.

The remaining five of the nine lock-gated roster sites (the bonus-release sites) re-accrue payroll only when an out-of-area bonus lock is released, so the prod-652 shape (a no-show off a completed no-bonus event keeps their line) recurs through them.
The 7/07 add-on cleanup removed proposal_addons and snapshot.addons but missed snapshot.breakdown, leaving 'Additional Bartenders (N)' lines on proposals 597, 605 and 608.
CC transfers were imported confirmed with the deposit as external_paid and no Balance invoice, so open_invoice_token was null, no Pay button rendered and balance reminders dead-ended.
