what: Manual orphan-payment link recomputed amount_paid but did not call suppressStaleBalanceReminders, so pending balance-due reminders could still fire on a now-paid proposal
admin/payroll.js selected bartenders with an un-trimmed LOWER(sr.position) = 'bartender' while the accrual filter trims, so the admin payroll screen and accrual could disagree on who is a bartender.
Staff could set Zelle as their preferred pay method but ALLOWED_PAY_METHODS omitted zelle, so mark-paid rejected Zelle payouts (latent prod bug).
Until pr-c shipped, Zelle mark-paids from the old UI recorded a null handle (zero such rows found in prod).
The admin Overview payroll figures counted owner no_draw money as owed.
PATCH /admin/payroll/payout-events/:id recomputes wage only and never re-splits tips, so a line zeroed to hours 0 keeps a non-zero card_tip_net_cents.
Client lifetime value sums proposals.amount_paid, which by design excludes service-extension money, so each client's LTV is understated by exactly their extension payments (accepted and left as-is).
SYRUP_NAME_LOOKUP lacked the renamed vanilla-bean, demerara and orgeat syrup slugs.

A client who removes Lab additions after paying the Lab invoice is silently over-collected: nothing refunds or flags it (until shopping-list re-approval), so the money is retained until an admin refunds it by hand.
Pay-then-add lab delta invoices list the cumulative lab set with the drift folded into the last line, so amount_due is exact but the line labels and amounts are warped.
The lab GET still offered a syrup already priced into pricing_snapshot.syrups, which then billed $0.
The Lab fold's syrup legs were not contract-preserving, so a contract syrup could be lab-added and then removed to shave it off the contract (latent, 0 prod rows).

The Lab PUT builds offeredSyrupByDrink from plan.pricing_snapshot while the fold reads the freshly locked proposal.pricing_snapshot, so the offer and the fold can price contract syrups from different snapshots (0 v2 proposals affected).
The lab and drink-plan submit writers stored a raw add-on count into proposal_addons.quantity instead of the engine-output shape every other writer and reader uses.
A client lab save re-prices an existing add-on line at the current catalog rate because its upsert recomputes line_total from service_addons.rate, not the frozen row rate.

A drink-plan 'pay now' extras submit got its invoice only on webhook success, so an abandoned card (requires_payment_method, no webhook) left the syrups committed in selections and on the shopping list with no invoice or payment row, and extras went uncollected on 3 prod proposals (regression from 772c337).

Drink-plan submit raised total_price and pricing_snapshot (bar rental, chargeable add-ons) without reconcileProposalPaymentStatus or createAdditionalInvoiceIfNeeded, so a fully paid proposal gaining extras stayed Paid in Full while owing and the delta was billed nowhere.

Drink-plan submit prices catalogAfter from the client's current selection while catalogBefore carries the snapshot syrups, so deselecting an already-contracted syrup without marking it self-provided yields a negative delta that shaves the negotiated total_price_override.

A client drink-plan submit carrying an add-on or bar re-priced the proposal from catalog and wrote total_price while leaving total_price_override stranded, so proposal 600's negotiated Check Cherry contract jumped to catalog and its balance would have overbilled the client $627.
On hosted non-mocktail packages a client drink-plan submit with zero resolved mocktails clears both pair rows, removing an admin-seeded Mocktail Bar add-on (accepted as picks-are-authoritative).

A v2 client who removes all mocktail picks after an admin reset-to-draft keeps the previously-flipped pair add-on billed until an admin removes it, because client submits never strip pair rows and the fast path never reconciles them.
The potion planner's mocktail flip could bill items the submitting UI never disclosed, closed by a version and contents gate.
The mocktail pair reconcile ran before the override baseline, mis-ordering the price override.
Drink-plan submit's reprice had the same dropped-quantity bug, rarely firing because its reprice is conditional.

A client drink-plan submit re-prices an existing add-on line at the current catalog rate because its upsert recomputes line_total from service_addons.rate instead of the rate frozen on the row, so a catalog price rise reaches proposals sold at the old price (aggregate l1-20, which also names the Lab upsert, folded here; the Lab instance is f1-148).
Drink-plan submit and Lab upserts rewrote line_total without the row's rate column, so a proposal_addons row's rate disagreed with its own line_total.

The drink-plan submit upsert honors any active add-on slug in the client payload and its ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE overwrites quantity with a one-unit count, so a payload naming a slug an admin set to 3 resets it to 1 (not reachable from the planner UI).
A paid_separately pay-now v2 submit with paid parking attaches no parking fee, so the fee is missed unless an admin adds it later (accepted revenue-miss).
A public v2 drink-plan submit without syrupSelections dropped the contract syrups and could net-lower total_price.
Legacy v1 drink plans skip the v2 submit tail, so they get no lab CTA, no lab follow-up and no parking-fee attach (open until the last v1 drafts submit and the legacy wizard is deleted).
After an on-site service extension, a drink-plan submit repriced the booking at the extended hours and re-billed the extension.

invoice_payments reversal rows carried no refund_id, so a partial refund on a payment that funded two invoices could not be attributed exactly (only a gross-clamp fallback) and displayed on every invoice the payment funded instead of only where it landed.

The plan's comp reconcile only voided the extras invoice, but an add-on pay-now submit folds add-ons, bar rental and new syrups into total_price through calculateProposal, so comping would leave total_price overstated.
The public invoice page showed a refund twice, once as a negative payment row and again as a refund row.

Voiding a Drink Plan Extras invoice defaulted to the comp semantic, subtracting it from total_price, which on a paid-in-full proposal invents an overpayment; reconcile_total was added to PATCH /api/invoices/:id with the Void UI.

Renaming an extension invoice away from 'Service Extension' double-counted money, because webhook keys skip on the label while settle keys on invoice_id, until the off-ledger guard was made symmetric.
record-payment wrote the raw admin-entered amount to the activity log instead of the capped amount actually applied, so an overpayment entry showed more paid than the ledger took
The record-payment receipt email reported the raw entered amount instead of the capped amount actually applied.
record-payment capped the proposal-side delta but credited the uncapped entered amount to the invoice, inflating invoices.amount_paid, wrongly locking the invoice and drifting the invoice ledger.
Admin record-payment linked a full outside payment to the open Deposit invoice the same way, stranding the remainder off the invoice ledger

The cancellation refund's charge query excluded the drink_plan_with_balance and drink_plan_extras payment rails although its refund target summed every payment, silently under-refunding and sending a false 'refunded in full' email.

applyRefundReconciliation decremented invoices.amount_paid while retainerCents read live from the Deposit invoice, so a second /cancel/refund run after a mid-loop failure computed a higher client-mode target (about +5% of retainer) and over-refunded.

After cancel, refund, restore, re-book, re-pay and re-cancel, the second cancellation's refund-cap snapshot sums all succeeded payments gross (refunds never demote payment rows), so the forfeited first-cycle retainer can leak back into the second refund cap.

cancel.js computed the retainer as SUM(amount_paid) WHERE label='Deposit', so relabeling deposits to Full Payment (and backfilling 24 rows) would have cancelled with retainer 0 and refunded about $95 of every $100 retainer; three other reviewers missed it.
fixed_ref: lane full-pay-invoice (breadcrumb-based retainer query, pinned in cancel.test.js)

what: Admin proposal edit (PATCH) skipped the bundle strip that create ran, so an edit could double-charge an add-on already included in the selected BYOB bundle
An edit that raised total_price above amount_paid left the proposal marked balance_paid.

An admin re-save (PATCH /:id) recomputes pricing_snapshot from catalog selections and rewrites proposal_addons, dropping hand-injected comp or discount lines; with total_price_override the total stays pinned but the itemized freebies vanish.

settleExtension moves event_duration_hours but not total_price or the pricing snapshot, and the admin PATCH re-prices every save from the row's duration, so an editor save on a booking with a settled extension bills the added hours again.

An admin duration change on a booking with total_price_override carries the override through and calculateProposal substitutes it, so added hours, over-included bartenders, time-priced add-ons and surcharges bill $0 (607 moved 5h to 6h adds $0 against $575 at catalog).

The new lifecycle archive reap fired from any source status, so a force-archive from completed would strip the approved-bartender roster that the tip clawback and late-tip roll-forward read, and a post-archive refund could not claw
The financials 'Collected' figure summed succeeded proposal_payments and never subtracted proposal_refunds, overstating collected money (prod true net $9,255 against $9,555 gross).
Per-row payments-list netting keyed on proposal_refunds.payment_id, so a refund with a NULL payment_id would reduce Collected with no matching row and the list would stop footing (latent).
The client's own 'Yours' compare card re-priced their bar instead of echoing total_price, so any catalog or pricing-regime drift showed a number contradicting the proposal printed above it
The contract-total echo was gated on today's rule check, so catalog or rule drift would show a legitimately sent proposal the client is being asked to pay as impossible

The current option's exemption from the client-visibility gate applied only on first load, so any re-quote dropped admin-only add-ons (parking fee, glassware above 100 guests) and the 'Yours' card got cheaper than the printed total

The shift-request upsert on a re-request reset status to pending but left dropped_at set, so the auto-assign scheduler seated a dropped staffer who then worked the shift and was paid nothing (accrual keys on dropped_at IS NULL).

POST /shifts/:id/assign (ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE) flipped a dropped staffer back to approved without clearing dropped_at, so they looked assigned but were invisible to roster math and paid nothing for the shift.

Denying an already-approved staffer re-accrues payroll only when an out-of-area lock moved, so a no-show denied off a completed no-bonus event keeps their wage and tip line and card tips stay split N ways (the prod-652 shape).
Approving a shift request re-accrues payroll only when an out-of-area lock moved, so a roster change on a completed no-bonus event leaves stale wage and tip lines.
Assigning a staffer (POST /shifts/:id/assign) re-accrues payroll only when an out-of-area lock moved, so a roster change on a completed no-bonus event leaves stale wage and tip lines.

The catch-all status UPDATE in the shift-request status handler has no payroll re-accrual hook at all, so a status change that takes someone off a completed event's roster leaves their wage and tip line payable.

DELETE /shifts/requests/:id (the ShiftDrawer Remove button) re-ran payroll accrual only when it also released an out-of-area lock, so a no-show removed after auto-completion kept her card-tip share on a pending payout (prod 2026-08-24, proposal 652 / shift 369: a $2.35 share kept, three bartenders each about $0.78 short)

Bar-rental shifts paid the bartender the $20 bar_rental duty derived from the booking while shifts.equipment_required stayed '[]', so the staff equipment card never listed the bar unless an admin hand-set it.

The paystub route early-returns the cached R2 PDF whenever paystub_storage_key is set, so the 9 already-issued paystubs kept rendering the wrong paid date after the date fix until their keys are cleared (after the deploy, never before).
A cover claim on a shift whose positions_needed parsed empty skipped the eligibility guard and could write a NULL or non-canonical position.
checkout.session.completed lacked the invoice integration (link, lock, balance invoice) that payment_intent.succeeded had
Tip webhook credited the bartender named in Stripe session metadata without checking the token's owner in payment_profiles, so an edited link or bad backfill could credit the wrong bartender
Invoice-type Stripe payments (public invoice page) were recorded but never rolled into proposals.amount_paid or status, so the proposal still showed the balance owed
Deposit paid through a Stripe Payment Link skipped the balance-reminder and pre-event-reminder scheduling that the PaymentIntent deposit path ran
Payment-link deposit settlement did not set proposals.payment_type.
The webhook did not distinguish full from deposit settlement for payment-link payments.

The payment webhook's full and balance branches set amount_paid = total_price with a forced status instead of additively crediting the amount actually charged with a derived status, so a mid-flight total change could mark a proposal paid in full at an amount the client never paid (a1-202's register-level additive-plus-derived-status item folded here; the remaining branches are m2-133).

The PI deposit branch and both Payment Link webhook branches set amount_paid to a flat total_price or deposit_amount instead of crediting the actual charge, and the amount_paid guards were not lifecycle-only, so a stale Payment Link could lose money and a deposit double-confirm was under-credited.

Refunding a true overpayment from the admin payment panel ran contract-scope reconciliation because POST /api/stripe/refund never passed a refund scope, so total_price fell with amount_paid and the proposal stayed overpaid while the contract shrank on every attempt (total 2300 / paid 2500, refund 200 left total 2100; prod 784 healed the same day).

create-intent persisted the client's skip-jar gratuity election into the proposal before payment, so an abandoned checkout left proposal 665 showing a $700 quote with a $250 gratuity line on four return visits
The webhook balance branch's zero-row status guard left proposals.amount_paid short when the proposal had already left deposit_paid, a phantom Outstanding (M3).
Refunds issued from the Stripe Dashboard reconciled through the webhook but never emailed the client, unlike in-app refunds.

The checkout.session.completed proposal-settle branch sets amount_paid from its own figure without asserting it matches session.amount_total (the tip branch does guard, at checkoutSessionCompleted.js:80), so a capture that differs from the expected amount is recorded wrong.
m2: Stripe payment-link payments (both link types) lacked the last-minute handling the main payment path applies.
The admin payment-link webhook (checkout.session.completed, payment_type full) used the same label-blind deposit link and would strand a full payment's remainder off the invoice ledger the same way

Label-blind oldest-open-invoice linking credited a pay-in-full on a deposit-terms proposal to the send-time $100 Deposit invoice capped at its remaining due (Sentry invoice_link_overflow_capped), so the payment_intent.succeeded path recorded $100 of a $550 payment and left the rest off the invoice ledger (25 prod proposals by shape); aggregates a1-58, m4-102 and m1-105 folded here, with the payment-link and record-payment entrances kept separate as c3-21 and c3-22 and the unrun row backfill as l1-30.
The webhook invoice branch rolled an off-ledger (Enhancement Lab) invoice payment into amount_paid and promoted balance_paid, forgiving the contract by its amount and silencing reminders.

paymentIntentSucceeded checks the gratuity floor against the current proposal row instead of the floor the PaymentIntent was created under, so clearing a sub-$50 mandate while a no-tip-jar client holds a live intent skips the already-charged gratuity as below_floor and DRB keeps tip money no bartender receives.

The full and deposit credit UPDATEs exclude status 'confirmed', so a capture on a proposal an admin advanced to confirmed with its Deposit still open records the payment row but never increments amount_paid, leaving a phantom balance (the balance branch had been fixed earlier)
A Stripe-dashboard refund on a partially overpaid proposal lands contract scope and over-shrinks total_price by the excess portion (Sentry warning; admin corrects in the editor).

The added-time rate printed under the Total on signed proposals and billed by computeExtensionDelta is read from the live service_packages row and never frozen at signing, so changing a package's extra-hour rate re-prices every client who already signed.

additionalTimeRate.js returns no added-time line for a class before reading the rate while the extension bill has no class exemption, so the day a class gets an extra-hour rate its extension bills it and the signing page prints nothing.

If the additional-bartender catalog row ever gets a minimum_hours, the pre-fold writers (submit.js, lab.js, and the cancel-line write-back) store max(hours, minimum) while the fold inverts by hours, latching the row at two bartenders: gratuity staff count doubles and syncShiftsFromProposal creates a second shift.
autoAssign's 'empty ranked list means any role' shortcut rewrote a committed Banquet Server row to Bartender, moving a server into the payroll tip split.
autoAssign counted bartender seats with bare LOWER(position), disagreeing with the trimmed comparison used by accrual (B14).
autoAssign.js lets a ranked list left from an older request win on a cover claim, so a Barback's claim can be auto-seated as Bartender (a different pay position) with no cover cascade.
drink_plan_with_balance PaymentIntents settle the balance but were invisible to the autopay guard's payment_type === 'balance' check, so autopay could charge a balance already being paid.

priceProposedState re-prices a proposal's existing add-ons with safeAddonQty(quantities[id]), which returns 1 for undefined, so the client-portal change-request price preview silently drops any count above 1 and under-quotes.
changeRequests buildDiff compares the stored output quantity against a proposed input count (unreachable today because the v1 form sends no addon_ids).
The invoiceSend comms action rendered the invoice's gross amount_due instead of the remaining balance (amount_due minus amount_paid) in the client send.
The cover-approval cascade re-accrues payroll only when an out-of-area lock moved, so a cover swap on a completed no-bonus event leaves the replaced staffer's wage and tip line in place.
coverBroadcast bucketed roles with bare LOWER(position), disagreeing with the trimmed comparison used by accrual (B14).

Pay-now drink-plan extras price non-flat add-ons (per_staff parking, per_100 garnish, per_guest_timed mocktail) flat while calculateProposal folds them at their real rate, so comping an unpaid such extra leaves a total_price residual of about $20-40.
Duty-line reconcile would remove admin-added duty lines for staff still on the roster.
eventCreation.js hardcodes STAFFING_ADDON_MIN_HOURS = 4 instead of reading the catalog, so its headcount divisor agrees with the other sites only while banquet-server and barback read exactly 4.0.
Once quantities stay at contract hours, eventCreation.js would divide them by worked hours and drop a staffing seat (three bartenders on a 4h-to-5h booking derive two) (design blocker).
Real-rate extras lines written without source_type 'addon' would make comp's hasAddonOrBar false and silently bring back the total_price residual.
Drink Plan Extras invoice line labels were built from post-mutation state, so they did not match the invoice's amount_due.

Invoices carry no record of whether their money sits inside proposals.total_price, so every derivation and overpayment classifier is a proxy, and three implementations (un-netted, netted by not-in-contract labels, the current closed label list) have each been wrong on a different real prod row, over- or under-refunding (provenance-first redo queued).

IN_TOTAL_PRICE_LABELS is a closed list of the five generated labels while POST /api/invoices/proposal/:id and PATCH /api/invoices/:id accept free-text labels, so a paid free-text invoice carrying contract money (proposals 596 and 547) is netted out as off-contract and under-refunded.
Invoice refresh regenerated non-standard invoices (e.g. Additional Services) from the proposal, clobbering their manual line items

invoiceHelpers read base_total and extra_bartender_cost, names the pricing snapshot no longer used (base_cost, staffing.total), so package and staffing lines were silently omitted from every auto-generated invoice
findOpenInvoiceForBalance could pick the Deposit invoice, so balance payments were absorbed into it and closed it prematurely
linkPaymentToInvoice locked partially paid invoices, freezing them before later add-on or balance changes could flow through

proposals.deposit_amount is dead in the charge path (create-intent selects it but charges the STRIPE_DEPOSIT_AMOUNT constant) while invoiceHelpers reads it for the Deposit invoice, so editing it (for example to 0) still charges $100 and desyncs the Deposit invoice.
A payment exceeding one invoice's remaining due is capped and Sentry-alerted (overflow_capped), but the overflow is not represented anywhere in the invoice sub-ledger (codex I1/I2).
createInvoiceOnSend counted VOID invoices, so a recovered (archived, draft, re-sent) proposal minted no fresh invoice on re-send and its payments went unlinked.
refreshUnlockedInvoices re-billed external_paid on Balance and Full Payment invoices for transferred events, minting invoices for the wrong amount.
createInvoiceOnSend did not net external_paid.
refreshUnlockedInvoices rebuilds an unlocked invoice's line items from the snapshot on any admin save, destroying a hand-built itemization (proposal 600's invoice within 7 minutes).
Any hand-built proposal set confirmed with a deposit but no invoice hits the same no-Pay-button dead end.
refreshUnlockedInvoices counted off-ledger invoices in lockedTotal, so the Balance refresh subtracted lab charges from the contract balance.

With a quiet default and no later-send, an edit that grows a payable invoice or an autopay charge would reach the client with no notice, since the gratuity staffing-change email is the only disclosure.
The invoice-derivation rewrite derived every unlocked label, so owed=0 zeroed and voided syrup-only extras invoices and admin-created manual invoices, deleting their line items.

refreshUnlockedInvoices skips every label except Deposit/Balance/Full Payment, so a price decrease strands Additional Services, Drink Plan Extras and Enhancement Lab invoices at the old amount (live over-billings on proposals 491, 556, 557).

createAdditionalInvoiceIfNeeded mints an Additional Services invoice for the full newTotal minus oldTotal without reading amount_paid, so on an already overpaid, fully locked proposal it bills the client for money DRB already holds.

The first post-cutover bookings skipped createInvoiceOnSend and never got an invoice; proposal 54 was repaired, and the later prod check found three more fully paid proposals (21, 59, 595) whose money came through payment rows with no invoice, a records gap with no money missing that was closed as an answer rather than repaired.

A pay-in-full on deposit terms left the send-time Deposit invoice at $100 and the rest off the invoice ledger (code fixed a784a578), but the row backfill never ran, so 26 paid receipts (e.g. INV-0329, INV-0336) still read 'Deposit $100' and a refund walks only the linked $100.

generateLineItemsFromProposal itemized invoice lines at catalog from the snapshot and add-on rows without folding total_price_override (or hidden adjustments) into the package line, so an overridden proposal's invoice lines did not add up to its total (INV-0120: $450 of lines on a $270 invoice).
Two of the three contract-payment link copies lacked the off-ledger label exclusion (it had reached only one rail on 2026-08-03), so an open Service Extension invoice could absorb a contract payment

A Full Payment invoice minted at send is linked at payment by linkOpenContractInvoice, which caps the credit at amount_due minus amount_paid with no re-derivation, so a gratuity elected at checkout may land as overflow instead of on the invoice (untraced; no prod instance).
A 2026-07-24 checkpoint change stopped writing proposal_addons.quantity in the cancel-line post-fold sync, made on the wrong belief that the column holds a raw count.
Under overpayment scope, dropping only amount_paid on a locked invoice left a client-visible phantom balance; locked invoices must drop amount_due too.
A cancel-line gratuity-removal refund passes no gratuityCents, so proposal_refunds.gratuity_cents is NULL for the one cancel kind the column exists to describe.

The cancel-line partial-removal write-back dispatches on billing_type while the reader dispatches slug-first, so if additional-bartender's catalog row ever left per_hour a partial cancel would store a raw count the reader divides by hours and the post-fold sync would cement it (unreachable today: nothing updates service_addons).

computeCancelTargets' lone-match branch binds the additional-bartender remove button to the num_bartenders override row's amount when a stale pricing_snapshot holds that row without the add-on row (identical labels); zero prod instances, producible only by manual SQL that changes num_bartenders without a fresh snapshot.
A partial removal of a lab-owned add-on leaves its labAdded entry in drink_plans.selections, so the client's next lab save re-upserts it at the lab quantity and undoes the removal.

reconcileOpenDeltaInvoices (cancel-line step 6) replaces an unlocked Drink Plan Extras invoice's addon and bar-rental lines with one synthetic manual line whenever its amount moves, deleting the source_type='addon' rows that are the only record of whether it folded into total_price, so extrasLinesAreFolded, the netting and the comp reconcile misclassify it permanently.

reconcileOpenDeltaInvoices collapsed open, unfolded syrup-only 'Drink Plan Extras' invoices because DELTA_LABELS wrongly asserted all three labels fold into total_price, destroying an uncollected receivable.
lineItemCancel.js writes a partial removal's remaining quantity at the row's worked hours, which the next contract-hours read would undo (design blocker).
CONTACT_AGGREGATES restates the paid-status literal instead of using the exported PAID_STATUSES, so the two can drift.
Dashboard qMoney and qRevenue metrics summed succeeded payments without subtracting refunds.
The new M5 orphan-line sweep would have deleted negative clawback debt lines along with orphaned worker lines.
M1's new invoice credit cap made capped contract payments look non-contract to M4's fee-share query, misallocating the contract fees staff gratuity bears.
A contract refund above roughly 90% after delivery can over-pay gratuity, because accrual computes gratuity from the immutable pricing_snapshot rather than the refunded total.
Accrual upserted only current workers and never deleted lines, so denied, unassigned or deleted workers kept payable wage, gratuity and tip lines (M5).
payrollAccrual.js filtered the tip pool with an inline toLowerCase() === 'bartender' that skips the shared isBartender() trim, so a whitespace-padded position would be excluded from the tip pool.
The accrual orphan sweep deleted an off-roster worker's line including a positive hand-entered reimbursement, which silently vanished whenever accrual re-ran.

Payout lines seed rate_cents from the profile only on first accrual and nothing flags a line rate that disagrees with the current profile rate, so user 212 was underpaid $15 on payout 82 when the agreed rate had never been entered.

A review bounty confirmed while no open pay_periods row covers today is never materialized when the period opens, because payrollAccrual never calls materializePendingReviewLines and only the next review confirm does, so two confirmed $10 bounties sat owed on prod with no screen or payout carrying them.

When a refund runs (POST /api/stripe/refund/:id, where refundExecute calls maybeReaccrueForDuty), accruePayoutsForProposal skips payroll re-accrual if the event's pay period is no longer open, and wages have no deferral marker to retry from, so refund-driven pay changes for closed periods are silently dropped (15 events 2026-08-11 to 2026-09-22).

On charge.dispute.funds_reinstated (dispute won) nothing rewound tips.refunded_amount_cents, so a later genuine refund on the same tip computed a zero delta in clawbackTip and silently under-clawed (F5).
payrollClawback selected bartenders with un-trimmed LOWER(sr.position)='bartender' while accrual trims, so a whitespace-padded position diverged between accrual and clawback.

The clawback ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE recomputed line_total with the pre-hold formula (no held_state awareness), so a remove, re-approve, tip-refund chain could turn a HELD reimbursement into payable money while it stayed flagged held, breaking paystub footing (B4).
Cancel-time clawback could over-claw a tip that was never accrued.

The cancel-path frozen-period clawback deferral retry replays without opts, so by then the shift_requests are denied, the pre-denial bartender list is lost and the marker advances with zero clawed (near-unreachable defense-in-depth path).
payrollDisputeNotify selected bartenders with un-trimmed LOWER(sr.position)='bartender' while accrual trims.

payrollLateTip.js kept a per-line GREATEST(0, ...) floor after clawback and accrual dropped theirs, so a late tip rolling onto a row carrying a negative cross-period clawback re-floored the debt to 0 (H1 residual every lane review missed).

The late-tip ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE recomputed line_total with the pre-hold formula (no held_state awareness), so a late tip landing on a held payroll row could make the held reimbursement payable while it stayed flagged held (B4).
payrollLateTip selected bartenders with un-trimmed LOWER(sr.position)='bartender' while accrual trims, so a padded position split the accrual and late-tip denominators.
payouts.total_cents was written independently at six sites, so new duty lines would leave payout totals inconsistent; recomputePayoutTotal became the single writer.

A card tip matched to a shift after accrual in a still-open period never paid out because the webhook path set shift_id but skipped accruePayoutsForProposal, and it was invisible on every admin surface (H2).
On CC-era transferred events the ghost $50 first-bar line reappears in the proposal-page breakdown after every admin save, though the override pins the total.

The balance-fold loaded add-on rows via a bare SELECT sa.*, dropping proposal_addons.quantity, so per_hour add-ons (additional-bartender, banquet-server, barback; prod quantities up to 6) repriced as quantity 1 and the first lab save of a native proposal under-billed by shaving total_price.

withRepriceQuantities dispatches on the catalog billing_type (REPRICE_ADDON_SQL selects sa.*) while both cancel-line queries dispatch on the frozen pa.billing_type, so an add-on whose catalog type was flipped after sale (as schema.sql did to parking-fee and garnish-package-only) reads as two billing types inside one transaction.

The fold could not recover the admin's unit count for per_guest add-ons, so one sold at count 2 repriced as count 1 and under-billed; the lane had deferred it on a 'no live row' premise that was false (proposal 482).

per_guest_timed add-ons are still excluded from count recovery because their line_total carries an extra-hours term (prod 464 reads 1.250 for a count of 1), so a touched row at count above 1 reprices at count 1.

REPRICE_ADDON_SQL does not select pa.variant, so a no-op fold drops the variant from snapshot.addons and a champagne-toast sold as non-alcoholic-bubbles reverts to 'Champagne Toast' on the client snapshot, after which the next writer persists variant null.

loadRepriceAddons inverted additional-bartender quantities at the worked hours of an extended booking, recovering two bartenders where three were booked (4h booking extended to 5h), so a reprice or cancel-line could drop a booked bartender.

Bundle-covered add-ons were stripped only on the client; the server twin mirrored just two of the bundle arrays, so a scripted or stale-tab POST could pay twice for add-ons a BYOB bundle already includes
Refund reconciliation lowered amount_paid but never re-derived proposals.status, so a refunded proposal stayed balance_paid or deposit_paid with money owed

Refund attribution took only amount and reason and walked invoices by invoice_id ascending, so a refund on a combined charge consumed contract invoices first, wrongly shrinking contract total_price and landing on the wrong invoice (M8).

issueRefund reversed the payment and invoice and downgraded proposal 500 to accepted but left its shift open (a bartender applied to the cancelled event), its balance invoice sent and dunnable, and 11 pending client reminders queued, because dispatcher suppression gated only on archived.
A refund spanning several invoices was not clamped and apportioned per invoice until multi-invoice refund clamping landed.
applyRefundReconciliation dropped amount_paid by the full refund including the off-ledger-linked portion that never entered amount_paid.
The EXCEEDS_AMOUNT_PAID guard in planRefund uses on-ledger amount_paid, so panel refunds of lab charges above on-ledger paid are rejected (dashboard refunds reconcile).

Refund dropDue keyed on 'is the invoice locked' instead of 'did refreshUnlockedInvoices rebuild its demand', giving unlocked non-total-tracking invoices a client-visible phantom balance on a live pay link (RC1).

The first overpayment fix derived excess as amount_paid - total_price, but Drink Plan Extras and manual-label invoices roll into amount_paid and never into total_price, so it subtracted them twice (a $150 refund on 2000/2150 left the total at 2000; a $1100 refund on 1000/1300 left a $100 phantom balance autopay would have charged) and made multi-split loops order-dependent.

A tip refund has no gratuity scope, so it lowers total_price and the override as contract money, and a later cancel-line 'remove gratuity' re-prices to override plus 0, reads the already-refunded tip as overpayment and offers to refund it a second time.

A refund lowered total_price and amount_paid but not total_price_override, so the next proposal-editor save carried the stale override forward and minted an Additional Services invoice for exactly the refunded amount (prod proposals 599 and 527)

Design stage: reversing credited invoice money for overpayment cents that were never on an invoice would have left a locked invoice demanding money on an unchanged contract; overpayment scope now consumes uncredited headroom first.

A contract refund on a booking with no override lowered total_price but wrote no line, so the next editor save recomputed the total from the lines and billed the refund again (proposal 847 and six other bookings carried the gap; backfilled by the 2026-10-19 conversion).

The admin's 'email a refund notice?' answer is held only in the request body and never stored on the proposal_refunds row, so the stale-pending sweeper emails the client unconditionally when it adopts a row and the refund.created handler stays silent, overriding a 'no' or dropping a 'yes'.
Notify drafts composed with money figures at preflight would be stale, because rescheduleProposalInTx moves balance_due_date in-transaction and the autopay sweep keys on (proposal, balance_due_date).

computeExtensionDelta reads no signature column, so a v3 signer (promised $100/hr lead plus $40/hr per extra bartender on the final invoice) is quoted the v4 formula on a separate invoice whose terms say 'same terms'.

Extension gratuity silently never reached payroll when auto-complete accrual ran before the settle (grace-window payments near event end, the norm); the settle tail and heal now re-run accruePayoutsForProposal.

The extension heal re-runs accrual only when applyExtensionHours reports touched lines, so a crash after the hours applied but before accruePayoutsForProposal leaves the extension gratuity addend at $0 until something else recomputes accrual.

The cancel-time bartender capture used bare LOWER(position) while accrual trims, so a padded ' Bartender' row was paid a tip share but excluded from the clawback, burning the marker with nothing clawed or over-clawing the clean bartender (B14, cancel site).

addSelfProvidedSyrups pushes every self-provided syrup onto the client's shopping list without checking the proposal's comped or paid syrups (pricing_snapshot.syrups.selections), so a client is told to buy a syrup DRB is already supplying (re-diagnosis of the audit's suspected syrup-picker cross-check bug; the money path does cross-check).

autoGenerateShoppingList never joins service_packages and shoppingListGen.js has no hosted concept (serving_type defaults to full_bar), so hosted proposal 728 got an auto-generated list stocking the full BYOB premium par.
matched_kind stays stale when a linked money row is hard-deleted: the link goes NULL but the kind does not change.

The payout sweep's stuck-line alarm reports Stripe payout lines that match no succeeded proposal payment, tip, or refund row for more than 7 days, and the count keeps growing (4 through 2026-10-09, then 7, 10, and 12 by 2026-10-14, still 12 on 2026-10-19; 130 events since 2026-07-09).
The staff paystub and Pay tab show a held amount that is excluded from totals (dispute risk).
The v2 planner recorded parking as free text, so clients could not buy parking at all.
The cancel-flow spec mixed dollar and cents money sources until cents-only sources were pinned.

The invoice page's Refunds block showed a refund against a payment that funded two invoices at its full amount on both invoices (deferred as rare when the block shipped, clamped per invoice by the F3 fix 5e9c9d34, then exactly attributed per refund in c89fe834).
Admin home dashboard computed booked, collected and outstanding totals client-side from /api/proposals, which returns at most 50 rows, so totals were wrong once proposals exceeded the page
ProposalCreate pricing dock showed the deposit as 50% of the total, but the actual deposit is a flat $100
ProposalCreate lost the package-slug add-on exclusion (PACKAGE_EXCLUDED_ADDONS), so The Clear Reaction could be sold mocktail-bar and pre-batched-mocktail add-ons it already includes (regression)
The admin quote builder formatted add-on rates with whole-dollar fmt$, rounding fractional NUMERIC rates ($0.50 bottled water, $1.50 cups, $0.75 extra hour) to "$1" and similar.
Admin proposal edits re-derived the gratuity rate even when gratuity was not edited.
Pre-catalog editor saves PATCHed empty addon_quantities, which the server defaults to 1, underpricing add-ons.
The merged event editor collapsed num_bartenders overrides on every save, silently dropping charged over-ratio bartenders.
A blank guest_count in the proposal editor previewed pricing at 50 guests but PATCHed 0.

The v1 planner's LogisticsStep previews the per_staff parking fee as rate times bartenders while the server bills it over all staff (bartenders, additional bartenders, barbacks, servers), so live v1 plans under-quote parking (plan 69 / proposal 472 previewed $40, billed $60).
Paid-in-full banner compared amount_paid to total_price exactly, so float cents drift could hide it (no 1-cent tolerance)
The ProposalView paid card showed total minus a hardcoded $100 instead of the true balance.
The client change form turned a deliberate num_bars=0 into a phantom bar charge.
A staffer (user 212) was paid $20/h instead of $22/h for 7.5h on payout 82, corrected with a $15 manual ledger row.

Specialty alcohol add-ons (bitter aperitifs, vermouths, liqueurs, mezcal, cognac) were seeded applies_to 'all', so BYOB and mocktail proposals could be sold alcohol add-ons that only apply on the hosted path
After H1 removed line floors, the admin payout-line PATCH still floored lines at 0, which would have re-buried clawback debt on an edit.
The shipped client-portal change-request preview calls priceProposedState without num_bartenders, so an admin staffing override is re-derived from the 1:100 ratio in the preview (unfixed there).
Drink-plan submit charged auto-added upgrade add-ons without checking that a triggering cocktail was still selected or that the package already covered them
A pay-then-add Lab delta invoice lists the cumulative Lab set with the price drift folded into the last line, so amount_due is exact but the client-facing line amounts and labels are wrong.

The extras fold loaded add-on rows via bare SELECT sa.*, dropping proposal_addons.quantity, so every per_hour add-on repriced as quantity 1 and shaved extras off total_price on the first (even empty) lab save of a native proposal.
The lab fully-paid remainder subtracted locked 'Drink Plan Extras' pay-now money that is not in total_price, under-billing the remainder.
In the fully-paid case the lab invoice billed the full remainder without subtracting other open contract invoices, double-billing Additional Services (fleet round 1).
The lab pre-fold writer bypasses addonQuantity.js and stores max(duration, minimum_hours) x count while the reader divides by raw hours, the same latent 2x additional-bartender latch.

The first override-preservation fix differenced the drink-plan catalog delta from the engine total including the client-gratuity line, so an add-on that moved the gratuity basis (for example an additional bartender) baked gratuity into total_price_override and charged it twice (verified $200 overcharge: $360 shipped vs $160 true).
Marking an already-contracted syrup self-provided was stripped from only one override-delta leg, pushing a negative delta that shaved the negotiated contract on a public route.

The drink-plan submit pre-fold writer bypasses addonQuantity.js and stores max(duration, minimum_hours) x count while the slug-first reader divides by raw event hours, so once additional-bartender gets a minimum_hours a one-bartender order latches at two (double gratuity staff count and a second shift); latent, trigger not fired in prod (the aggregate line c3-144 naming the submit and lab writers is folded here; the lab writer is f1-155).
Drink-plan submit once priced from request-body inputs instead of reading every pricing input off the proposal row (the '$627 failure' class).
Invoice line_total was taken from the request instead of computed server-side from quantity and unit price
The package margin sketch uses || fallbacks, so an explicit 0 labor rate, supplies setting or slider value is treated as unset.
The package margin sketch holds flat-package revenue constant while labor cost scales with extra hours, understating margin erosion.
Public quote submit honored a Top Shelf class flag on non-class packages, letting a scripted client create $0 drafts for premium packages
Admin proposal PATCH accepted any total_price_override (negative, NaN or unbounded)

POST /:id/cancel/refund recomputed its target from live state its own refunds mutate (the Deposit invoice amount_paid), so a retry raised the target and issued a fresh Stripe refund of about 0.95x the deposit cents already reversed (B5).
Across a cancel, restore, re-cancel cycle the cancel-refund snapshot uses a gross SUM, so the retainer can leak into the refund target (accepted residual of B5).

The B5 fix caps the refund but keeps the live target, so a retry after partial reconciliation can under-refund when the gratuity-funded gate flips false (FLAG 3; replacing the target needs an owner call).
A refund with a NULL payment_id was netted out of Collected but attached to no ledger row, so the ledger rows silently failed to add up to Collected.
The Financials 'Collected' total summed gross succeeded payments and never subtracted refunds.
The 'Payments in range' ledger LEFT JOIN invoice_payments fanned each refunded payment into duplicate full-value rows (the ledger summed $10,205 against a true $9,255).
The financials ledger per-row net_amount could render negative on an over-refunded row until clamped with GREATEST(..., 0).
Public calculate and submit fed client-supplied addon_quantities into pricing unbounded, so negative, fractional or huge quantities could shift the price

Compare-options pricing fed proposal_addons.quantity (an output column) back in as an input multiplier, so per_guest add-ons multiplied by guest count twice (an $850 BYOB proposal quoted at $10,350 on dev; up to 20x on the 11 prod proposals carrying them).
April legacy proposals with null snapshots still move across a re-quote on dev (prod has zero of that class); the delta-anchoring fix was logged, not built

The current option's exemption from the add-on visibility gate applied only on first load, so a client toggling anything silently dropped their own hidden add-ons (parking fee, over-100-guest glassware) and the 'Yours' card priced below the total printed above it.
Stripe webhook apportioned drink-plan extras and balance cents from metadata without clamping to intent.amount, so corrupted metadata could apportion more than was charged

A Stripe-dashboard refund on a partially overpaid proposal is reconciled with binary contract scope and over-shrinks total_price by the excess portion, leaving only a Sentry warning for the admin to correct.
storedToInputCount disagreed with the engine's slug-first, raw-hours handling of additional-bartender minimum_hours (closed in-lane after the Task 1 review).
The client-portal change-request price preview re-prices existing add-ons through safeAddonQty, which returns 1 for an undefined count, so the preview silently drops any add-on quantity above 1.
priceProposedState silently dropped num_bartenders
The draft's settled-extension hours SUM lacked COALESCE, so a booking with no settled extension would read NULL (design blocker).

The Drink Plan Extras invoice drift adjustment folded rounding drift into the last line's line_total but left its unit_price stale when quantity was above 1, so unit_price no longer matched line_total on extras invoice lines.

Non-flat add-ons (per_staff parking, per_100 garnish, per_guest_timed mocktail) are priced flat in the pay-now Drink Plan Extras charge and invoice while calculateProposal folds them at their real rate, so comping an unpaid one leaves a total_price residual of about $20-40.
The real-rate extras spec computed the add-on delta at the natural post-UPSERT call site, where it would always be $0 (must be captured pre-UPSERT over the filtered set).

The second cancel-line overpayment implementation (in the reverted invoice-derivation rewrite) netted out every invoice whose label was not in CONTRACT_LABELS, under-refunding clients because Additional Services and Enhancement Lab money is inside total_price (wrong on a real prod row).
The first cancel-line overpaymentCents was un-netted, so it counted paid syrup and manual-label money as overpayment and over-refunded it through real Stripe refunds (wrong on a real prod row).
Drink-plan extras invoice line items were rounded per line, so their sum could differ from amount_due and the invoice showed a phantom balance
Drink-plan syrup cents were computed by subtraction, producing 1-cent ghost line items

createAdditionalInvoiceIfNeeded double-billed the delta in the common deposit_paid state because refreshUnlockedInvoices already folds it into the unlocked Balance invoice; the admin crud.js re-price path was affected too.
The derivation rewrite netted non-derivable open invoices out of the Balance remainder, under-billing the contract by their amount.

refreshUnlockedInvoices derives a Balance as total_price - external_paid - sum(locked amount_due), using locked invoices as a proxy for money collected, so proposal 51 with an unbacked $100 deposit was re-billed $1,100 against $1,000 owed on each re-price.

generateLineItemsFromProposal pushed every pricing adjustment unsigned while the pricing engine negates discounts, so a $50 discount printed as a +$50 charge on every invoice built from the snapshot and the lines summed to the total plus twice the discount (26 non-void invoices on 22 proposals measured 2026-10-08; line regeneration refused discounted proposals).
Win-rate cohort was not a true Won/Pending/Lost partition (cancelled-after-accept counted as won) and lost-value counted a phantom 'archived' status
Dashboard qMoney and qRevenue paid basis never subtracted refunds, disagreeing with the refund-aware qOutstanding by the refunded total.
qAccepted counted 214 proposals but summed value over 204, an $800 axis mismatch on the metrics.

Gratuity fee-netting summed Stripe fees from all succeeded payments (invoice and drink-plan extras rails) against a contract-only total_price denominator, under-paying staff gratuity on bookings with extra card charges (M4).
When the last bartender is removed while a barback or server stays on the roster, splitEvenly(x, 0) returns an empty list, so an already-matched card tip pays nobody and nothing warns.
A cross-period tip clawback line was inserted with line_total GREATEST(0, negAdj) = 0 while tips.refunded_amount_cents advanced, so the staff tip debt was never collected and replay no-oped (H1).
Clawback fee rounding was computed per delta instead of cumulatively, drifting about 1 cent per partial tip refund (L4).
Tips part-way through a partial-refund sequence when the L4 fix deployed can be off by 1 cent, because history was per-delta while the new formula is cumulative (accepted).
When a Stripe fee is captured after a same-period refund, the clawback adjustment is stale by cents (deferred).

payrollLateTip.js kept a per-line GREATEST(0, ...) floor on INSERT and ON CONFLICT after clawback and accrual dropped theirs, so a late-tip roll-forward onto a cross-period clawback row re-floored the debt to 0.
calculateBaseCost produced negative or nonsensical prices from zero or negative inputs
pricingEngine applied an inconsistent small-rate fallback for base_rate_3hr

Hosted per-guest packages charged hourly plus gratuity for additional bartenders (num_bartenders override and the additional-bartender add-on), though hosted pricing included them, and invoices carried those lines
After the hosted 1:100 bartender-ratio rule shipped, class packages (hosted, bar_type class) were charged hourly plus gratuity for over-ratio bartenders, though classes keep all bartenders free

calculateBarRental uses Number(pkg.first_bar_fee || 50), so an explicit 0 first_bar_fee still charges $50 per bar whenever num_bars is nonzero (the $400 trap, worked around with num_bars 0 on service-only drafts).
The 25-guest hosted minimum is real policy but pricingEngine.js does not enforce it (min_guests 50 is only the small-event rate threshold), so a 24-guest hosted quote goes through.
gratuityBasisFromSnapshot reconstructs the gratuity basis from legacy pricing snapshots by a lossy inverse, so a legacy booking's basis can come out wrong.
Passing totalPriceOverride straight to the engine replaces the whole computed total, so every extra prices at $0 (the obvious fix for the override bug gives money away).
deriveGratuityRate did not re-assert the floor on the derived rounded rate, so totals in [floor - 0.005, floor) charged and then 500-looped the webhook.

withRepriceQuantities fed the stored output quantity (effectiveHours x count) back as the engine's input for per_hour add-ons, so a no-op fold squared the hours (a $450 banquet-server line repriced to $2,700 in a prod-shaped probe); introduced when 6aa9a620 began carrying pa.quantity.

Add-on quantity inversion divided the contract-hours stored quantity by the worked duration and rounded, so three additional bartenders over a 4h-to-5h extension read as two while one reads fine, which fixtures with one bartender missed.
The lockedTotal invoice-label filter was not NULL-safe.
planRefund's EXCEEDS_TOTAL pre-check assumed every refund was contract money, so it rejected valid extra-scope refunds that do not reduce total_price
proposal_refunds.total_price_after was not floored at 0 while the live total_price column clamps, writing negative figures into refund history (L6).

05c38bb0's RC3 derived refund excess as amount_paid - total_price, which counts Drink Plan Extras and manual-label invoice money as excess and swallowed genuine contract refunds (multi-split loops became order-dependent); reverted the same day.

Refunding a true overpayment through the payment panel lowers total_price and amount_paid by the same amount, so the proposal stays overpaid and the contract silently shrinks on every attempt (2300/2500, refund 200, became 2100/2300); the netting term exists but is wired only into cancel-line.

Overpayment was computed as raw amount_paid minus total_price, ignoring paid off-contract invoices (Drink Plan Extras, manual) that roll into amount_paid but never total_price, flagging false overpayments (prod 599); the 2026-07-26 attempt was reverted for it.

applyRefundReconciliation clamps total_price and total_price_override at 0 independently, so gratuity dollars refunded beyond the override leave total minus override below the derived gratuity and the next re-price bills the gap (override 100 + gratuity 50, refund 120: next save bills 50).

The first overpayment-scope refund allowance named only one funding source (uncredited charge headroom vs contract-invoice slack) and refused the commonest overpayment, a contract repriced down after full card payment, after five lane reviewers passed it.
The active-staff count behind the fewer-than-3-staff-homes remote fee rule lacked a role IN (staff, manager) filter.
computeExtensionDelta did not throw on a negative delta from pathological pricing data.

Service extensions under or straddling the 4h base were priced as the catalog difference and booking discounts reduced the extension charge (3h to 5h billed $100 not $200; 3h to 4h billed $0 service, so proposal 842's paid prod extension collected only $25 gratuity), until the 2026-09-26 rule billed every hour past the booked end at the package extra-hour rate.
Extensions on class packages bill $0 for the class (owner decision open).

The shopping list put recipe-only rim garnishes (margarita salt, Tajin, sanding sugar) at 1 per 25 guests plus 1 per extra drink using them, landing four or more containers where one covers the event and the owner cut them to 1 on every approved list (a purchase quantity, not DRB money).
Recipe-derived shopping-list rows ignore par_items.qty_per_100 (flat ceil(guests / 25)), so a par quantity edit does nothing for non-baseline items; no taxonomy key covers non-money quantity math.
Auto-drafts never added the bar rental (num_bars 1, $400 total) when the lead asked DRB to bring the bar.
The Thumbtack auto-draft priced from a hardcoded 4 hours instead of the real event duration.

The service-extension automation bills agreement-v3 signers the v4 additional-time formula, which differs on hosted packages (every live v3 signer is on the Core Reaction, where both formulas agree; owner decision open).
