The admin profile PUT treated an omitted preferred_name as cleared, so a partial payload silently nulled a person's name across payroll, BEOs and the tip page.

calcom.js committed the webhook dedupe row before the handler ran, so a handler throw stranded the event and Cal.com's retry was skipped as already processed, losing consult creates, cancels, reschedules and no-shows.
A concurrent duplicate confirm double-emailed the client because the route sent without checking that the atomic side-effect flip had applied.

The Resend marketing webhook had no replay gate (no UNIQUE event key with ON CONFLICT), so a redelivered or concurrent event inserted a duplicate row and re-applied status, bounce and unsubscribe writes.

email_sends.status was set with a bare UPDATE and no monotonic guard, so an out-of-order Resend event (opened after bounced, delivered after opened) regressed the status and corrupted campaign analytics.
Marketing contact tag writes replaced the set without a row lock, so two admins saving different sets could interleave delete-then-insert and land on the union

marketingSend resolves the mailable set once at run start and the per-recipient loop never re-checks suppression, so someone who unsubscribes during a multi-minute campaign send (600ms pacing) is still mailed.

marketingSend's run claim (status <> 'sending' ...) also accepted an archived campaign, so a campaign archived between the send route's SELECT and its claim UPDATE was flipped back to 'sending' and mailed, and the losing 409 told the operator it was 'already sending'
Record-payment read currentPaid before its transaction and locked the clients row instead of the proposal, so a double-click or two admins created two payment rows and a doubled locked invoice (M7).
Record-payment re-reads the just-inserted payment with ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1 instead of INSERT ... RETURNING id, so concurrent inserts can link the wrong payment row to the invoice.
The admin archive endpoint locked the proposal before the client row and grouped settles locked loser rows before the sweep's client lock, AB-BA deadlock cycles under concurrency.

POST /shifts/:id/assign seats a person in an already-full role with no shift row lock or room re-check, so a second admin, a can_staff manager or the auto-assign scheduler can over-fill a shift (roster 2/1) and the tip split counts both.

The server's shift deny is an unconditional UPDATE and the drawer does not re-read before Deny or Remove, so a request approved in between by another admin or the auto-assign scheduler is denied after its approval text went out, and nobody is told.
create-intent-for-invoice minted a fresh payment intent per POST and linkPaymentToInvoice added uncapped with no status check, so a two-tab payment silently set amount_paid to twice amount_due (M1).

create-intent (the deposit and checkout rail) minted a fresh PaymentIntent beside a succeeded or processing one and both webhooks credit additively, so a reload of an unsettled accepted row, or a second entry while a bank debit settled, could take a second real charge; now 409 PAYMENT_IN_FLIGHT.

create-intent mints a second identical PaymentIntent when a pending election-bearing intent matches the request's amount and election exactly, leaving a window for a visible double payment (accepted by Dallas).
payment_failed was not monotonic against a succeeded intent, so out-of-order delivery sent a false 'payment failed' email and flipped the session to failed (L1).

The RC4 adopt-own-row-by-id fix reached refundExecute and the sweeper but not the charge.refunded webhook, which still adopted a pending refund row by the (intent, amount) heuristic although the row id rode in the refund metadata, so a stranded same-amount row of the other scope could be adopted.
The Thumbtack duplicate-heal from 7b01a78 used proposal_id as its never-ran marker, so a provider retry inside the lead-commit to draft-commit window re-ran the admin notify (B10).
The voice dead-leg alert dedup was check-then-act around an awaited Telegram send, so concurrent Twilio status callbacks both sent the 'call didn't connect' alert and both wrote audit rows (B11).

Auto-assign approved and texted without an atomic pending-to-approved claim (no AND status='pending'), so the manual route racing the hourly sweep could double-approve and send a duplicate approval SMS.

The new autopay prior-intent guard could miss a settling prior charge: it matched prior intents by amount, read only the newest row (LIMIT 1) so another intent could shadow it, and ignored intent status, so it neither excluded webhook-confirmed charges nor told a settling charge from a failed one.

The autopay double-charge guard counted only payment_type 'balance' intents, so a drink_plan_with_balance payment settling during a webhook outage was invisible and autopay could charge the balance again (B12); the predicate became payment_type 'balance' OR balance_amount_cents > 0.

If the payment_intent.succeeded webhook went undelivered over 24h, the autopay stale-claim TTL (24h, equal to Stripe's idempotency-key lifetime) let hour 25 fire a second off-session charge, and the uncapped additive balance credit recorded amount_paid as total plus balance (F1).
Email sequence sends had no claim keyed on current_step and email_sends had no unique (lead_id, sequence_step_id), so a step could double-send.

99fd240 widened scheduleEventEve's reschedule DELETE to 'processing' rows, erasing an in-flight dispatch's claim so its sent-marker no-oped and the re-insert fired a duplicate or lost T-24 client SMS (B9).
findOpenPeriodForDate (payrollProcessing.js:12) resolves the open pay period without row locking, a low-probability race left after mark-paid and finalize gained FOR UPDATE locks.

Pending refund-row adoption (applyRefundReconciliation) matched on (intent, amount), so a stranded same-amount pending row could be adopted by a later refund and decide its money semantics (RC4); refundExecute and the stale-pending sweeper now pass the row id.

The overpayment refund cap nets only pending overpayment-scope rows, so a concurrent contract-scope refund linked to a non-contract invoice or a cancel-line fold can consume the same excess and drop amount_paid below total_price, demoting status and disarming autopay.
The message dispatcher had no atomic send claim and its terminal UPDATE lacked AND status='pending', so overlapping ticks could double-send (CLAIMS batch).
processInboundSms short-circuited on bare twilio_sid row existence, so an opt-out, opt-in or CONFIRM/CANT side effect that threw after the message was recorded was lost on Twilio's retry.

handleCant reads the approved shift outside its transaction and denies with an unlocked, unconditional UPDATE, so two concurrent CANTs for one assignment both run, both reopen the shift and both notify.
The agent leased full first-reply batches into the remaining daily-cap slots, burning stranded jobs' attempts.
Saving a payroll adjustment's note and amount raced.
The cancel-flow spec ran clawback at cancel time without idempotency against the charge.refunded webhook, risking a double clawback.
The admin SW's navigation shell write failed unless the response was cloned synchronously before respondWith resolved (with waitUntil).
admin-sw.js names its per-user API cache from a message the app chrome posts on mount, and the first stored load can race that message and land in the wrong cache.
The desktop ShiftDrawer's Retry after a lost response re-posts the assign, texting and emailing the staffer a second time.
An edit made after a NETWORK_ERROR is replaced by the replayed first send: the retry reuses the send id, so the server replays the stored text and the edit is dropped silently.
As planned, a failure box outlived the action it belonged to, so Retry could repeat a stale staffing write.
EventEditForm omitted addon_quantities from its PATCH, so the server's safeAddonQty reset admin-set add-on quantities to 1; no taxonomy key covers an omitted field clobbering a stored value.
A moved-key Inbox deep link writes seen twice.

A fresh ComposeTab mount minted a new campaign id, emptying both server duplicate defenses, so following the quota panel's 'run this again tomorrow' or refreshing mid-send would re-mail everyone already reached
The draw toggle could be double-submitted until a submit hold was added.
The effect-synced detailRef lagged a render, so two same-frame line saves double-counted the first delta in the pay-run queue rollup.
RecipesTab wrote its cache under the live render's drink type, so a mid-debounce cocktail/mocktail switch landed a save in the wrong list or merged it onto a same-slug drink.

The admin edit form always sent tip_jar and gratuity_total, so an unrelated edit such as guest count silently shifted the client-elected gratuity rate; no taxonomy key covers an untouched field clobbering a stored value.
The payment receipt popup had no busy state, allowing a double submit.
A bare return on the acknowledged curfew retry let the outer finally re-enable Save mid-flight, allowing a duplicate PATCH and a duplicate client notify

Cancel-line adjustment targets are positional and the admin pages kept stale indexes after a save, so a confirm could remove (and refund) a different line; targets now reload after every save, two open tabs can still race.
ContestRail loads had no request sequencing, so a slow read for one quarter could render its standings under another quarter's label while the award paid winners recomputed from the current quarter.
A late async search answer wrote history while React 18 kept the old screen mounted during a lazy route load, rewriting the page the user had moved to.

On the Stripe return for a grouped proposal, /resolve still read the group as undecided (the webhook that decides it had not committed) and bounced the paying client to /compare, destroying ?paid=true before the settle state started
AddMethodModal spread its stale methods snapshot into the parent update, which could revert a payout handle changed on another device mid-session.
Sentry SERVER-10 recorded duplicate-key errors on client inserts, already fixed on HEAD by the time of the audit.
The handedOff path double-created its out-of-area record.
The pay-period lock's scoping does not match accrual order (pp-lock residual; detail not in memory).
Review of the fix-perim lane found perimeter alerts were not deduped by alerting reason.
The transfer apply had an enqueue-then-purge gap in which a running dispatcher could fire past-dated reminder rungs.

Concurrent gate runs both reset the shared Neon ci-smoke branch and deleted each other's rows mid-test, producing spurious money-suite failures and risking a receipt banked for a gate that never really ran
The gate lock path used --absolute-git-dir (per worktree) while the ci-smoke branch is global, so two lanes could each hold their own lock and reset the same branch

Stale gate-lock reclaim used a blind unlink, so two starters could both reclaim and run (reproduced 4 of 25 trials, once with three concurrent money gates); it survived the first lock rewrite until flock replaced it
Clearing the Historical-events box sent 0 (parseInt || 0), silently zeroing a backfilled seniority baseline; no taxonomy key covers a blank field clobbering a stored value.
sms_messages.twilio_sid index was not unique, so concurrent Twilio retries of one inbound SMS could both pass the SELECT dedup and insert duplicate rows
Scorecard updates did not refresh scored_by, so edits stayed attributed to the original scorer (update missed a dependent field; no key fits)

Orphan-payment link refund branch read its guards outside any lock and ran an unconditional cc_event_id UPDATE, so two concurrent admin clicks could both insert proposal_refunds rows (recorded as deferred tech debt; the flow was later deleted, never fixed)
The payroll line PATCH's lock set did not include the pay_periods row, racing period status changes (lock set widened).
toggle-draw did not survive its post-COMMIT row vanishing to the stub sweep
Process-finalize could race the un-parking of a no_draw payout (process-finalize un-park race).
The /process route can act on a stale period_status (race).
toggle-draw's idempotency target in the request body was filed as a residual (detail not in memory).
Duty POST locked only the proposal, not the pay period, so a concurrent Process flip could land payable money in a just-frozen period

The admin profile PUT protects only preferred_name between omitted and cleared, so a partial payload nulls phone, email, address and emergency contact (latent: the sole caller round-trips every field; phone feeds inbound-SMS sender resolution; partial-update semantics; no taxonomy key fits).
Cal.com booking client INSERT caught a 23505 race without a SAVEPOINT, so the follow-up re-SELECT hit 25P02 and the whole transaction rolled back, losing the consult row
The Cal.com webhook committed its dedupe row before running the handler, so a hard kill mid-handler stranded the consult mirror while the booking survived in Cal.com.

The Cal.com strand-heal reprocessed any redelivered event whose uid was absent from consults; after a reschedule renamed the uid, a redelivery created a duplicate consult at the abandoned slot (which the sweep would ring) and marked the genuine one skipped_cancelled.
Out-of-order Cal.com reschedule webhooks plus root-uid naming can revert a consult to a stale slot (confirmed-conditional, pushed as-is; Sentry warn follow-up on the fix list).
Auto-generated shopping list UPDATE was unconditional, so it could overwrite an admin's edited pending list that landed between plan submit and generation
PATCH /api/drink-plans/:id/status checked the finalize lock and then wrote without it, so a status change could land on a plan an approve had just finalized in another tab.
The Enhancement Lab invoice read was not FOR UPDATE and its UPDATE was not guarded on locked or status, racing the webhook's pay-and-lock.
The shopping-list PUT had the same check-then-act finalize-lock gap (lock checked, write unguarded); the lock moved into the UPDATE WHERE.
On a null coverage resolution the mocktail pair-DELETE removed admin-seeded pair rows on a client submit (write destroyed rows it did not own).
/confirm-email-change read the pending row outside its transaction lock, so a double confirm bumped token_version twice and wrote two audit rows.
The email-webhook heal re-run overwrote the original *_at stamps instead of COALESCE-preserving them.
cfd284a3's replay-skip keyed on row existence, so a delivery that 500'd after the dedupe INSERT stranded the event and its bounce or unsubscribe write forever.
Concurrent Resend redeliveries could both pass the processed re-check and run the heal-path side effects (no row lock).
email_leads.status still uses a bare, non-monotonic overwrite (left as cosmetic).
A successful Resend call followed by a transient failure of the status='sent' UPDATE lands in the catch and marks the row failed, so a later retry reclaims and re-sends to that recipient.
A campaign-send review-round fix that reclaimed stranded send claims re-opened the duplicate-send door.
Staff and admin tip-page PATCH treated preferred_payment_method '' (an unselected radio) as an explicit clear, wiping a previously set method (update clobbered fields; no key fits)
The admin push preference PATCH used read-modify-write and lost concurrent switch flips (now merged in SQL with col || patch).
A partial PUT to the admin packages router wiped the package's slots (write destroyed data not in the payload).
Onboarding payment re-submit set venmo, cashapp and paypal handles straight from the body, nulling previously saved tip handles left blank (update clobbered fields; no key fits)
Admin proposal PATCH returned a separate post-commit SELECT instead of the UPDATE's RETURNING row, so a concurrent write could be returned as this edit's result
Public proposal sign did SELECT-then-UPDATE, so two parallel sign requests could both pass the status check and overwrite each other's signature

record-payment reads amount_paid (currentPaid) before BEGIN to gate the client-lock hoist and same-client sweep, so a concurrent first payment could leave a stale 0; judged benign and documented as an accepted risk, not fixed.

POST /:id/cancel-line/preview runs the whole mutation under exclusive row locks and then ROLLBACKs, so a concurrent charge.refunded webhook blocks behind an admin preview and each preview burns SERIAL values.
Change-request decline and cancel wrote the status flip and the activity-log row outside a transaction (other: a multi-table write outside a transaction).
The change-request apply read was not locked FOR UPDATE.
The proposal PATCH read the row without FOR UPDATE, so concurrent PATCHes or a webhook could lose-update gratuity_rate, tip_jar or status.
The lifecycle archive reap had an archive-vs-restore race, closed by an in-transaction archived re-check under FOR UPDATE
Public quote submit did SELECT-then-INSERT on the client email, so two near-simultaneous submits could both miss and collide on idx_clients_email_unique
Shift PUT wrote '[]' for omitted positions_needed and equipment_required, silently wiping staffing and gear when an admin edited only a date or note (no key fits)
Shift PUT wrote event_date = $3 even when the field was omitted, violating NOT NULL and returning 500 (no key fits)
The approve, deny and assign out-of-area lock stamp and release run as separate autocommit statements, leaving a millisecond window (admin-only, pre-notification).
A same-value out-of-area bonus re-save that could not stamp a lock still rewrote attached_by and attached_at to whoever clicked and logged a from==to audit row
A staffer own request delete did not carry status pending in the DELETE, so it could remove a request approved meanwhile; now 409 request_changed.

Remove deletes only queued reminder rows, so a reminder already processing at that instant, or one stranded by a dispatcher crash and reaped back to pending ten minutes later, still goes to the removed staffer.
A Remove racing a second operator's re-assign of the same person deletes the new assignment's reminder, because the assign skipped its insert while the old rows still existed.
Two concurrent payment-link requests could both pass the reuse check and insert duplicate stripe_sessions rows
Generating a deposit Payment Link was not idempotent, so a double click created a second Stripe price and link for the same deposit
Client payment-failed email throttle was check-then-send-then-log, so concurrent Stripe payment_failed retries could both pass the 24h check and double-email the client

Payment Link checkout.session.completed only marked its stripe_sessions row succeeded inside the first-delivery branch, so when payment_intent.succeeded claimed first delivery the link row stayed pending and reusable
Payment-state exclusions in the webhook guards dropped a legitimate second intent's credit, so two same-amount deposit intents could capture $100 while crediting $0.
The PI balance webhook branch kept its positive guard status 'deposit_paid', the same double-confirm under-credit shape left unhardened.

While a bank debit was still processing amount_paid was unchanged, so create-intent-for-invoice computed the full balance again and minted a second intent beside the settling one; proposal 784 paid its $400 Balance twice by bank debit.
create-intent checked status before taking the row lock, so a webhook flip to paid in between let it rewrite total_price on a paid proposal.
The L1 out-of-order guard is check-then-act, so a truly concurrent succeeded and stale payment_failed pair can still send a false failure email within a millisecond window (accepted).
When Stripe's charge.refunded beats the route's own reconciliation, the webhook applies it and emails the client even though the admin chose don't-send, because that choice is never persisted.
payment_intent.payment_failed had no event-level idempotency, so a Stripe redelivery inserted a duplicate failed row and activity entry and re-sent the admin email.
The processing handler wrote its webhook_events ledger row outside the transaction, so a failed delivery left the row and Stripe retry was acknowledged as a duplicate and dropped.

The extension settle heal re-runs payroll accrual only when applyExtensionHours reports touched lines, so a crash after the hours apply but before accruePayoutsForProposal leaves the extension gratuity at $0 until something else recomputes.
The bridged-call flow did not write its call_audit record before attaching the Twilio CallSid (audit-before-attachCallSid ordering).
The Thumbtack lead webhook committed the lead before creating the draft proposal and notifying the admin, so a crash plus retry deduped as already processed and silently lost both.
When a Thumbtack draft fails persistently, the post-commit heal re-notifies the admin on each retry (accepted residual).
Identical harvest-failed POSTs each incremented the lead's attempt count.
Voice status callbacks had no (CallSid, CallStatus) dedup, so a redelivered 'failed' callback sent a duplicate Telegram alert.
The lead-call press-1 handler claimed the attempt before validating the request (fixed to validate-before-claim).
The lane draft autopay did not read in-flight bank debits, so the balance autopay could charge the card while a bank debit was still processing; the server fleet added the in-flight read.
Autopay scheduler and manual charge-balance had no atomic claim and no Stripe idempotency key, so concurrent runs or a manual click racing a tick could double-charge the balance

The audit's 'first five to check' list put balanceScheduler.js:77 alone and never named stripe.js:340, which builds the same autopay idempotency key; retargeting one would have diverged the keys and removed the only guard against a second real balance charge.
The dial-cap trip email fired only when COUNT(*) = 1, so two trips landing together both counted 2 and neither emailed, and a sustained attack never alerted
In the draft drip fix a surviving sibling that had already finished its own sequence could inherit the drip and be nurtured twice (found by /code-review, folded).
Two concurrent solo sends for the same client and event date can both pass the read-then-write sibling check and both enroll a drip; declined because advisory locks are a no-op on the Neon pooler.
The duty catch-up pass had no stable ORDER BY, so two admins confirming different reviews concurrently could interleave unique-index waits into a 40P01 deadlock
The event-details six-query fan-out is not one snapshot, so a drop committed mid-fan-out can make viewer.is_assigned and my_request_status transiently disagree.

A reschedule landing in the seconds-wide mid-send window whose send then hangs over 10 minutes gets reaper-redispatched with the hardcoded 'tomorrow' copy for an event now days out (accepted residual).
The 3-minute sweep could ring a lead seconds after a reply confirmed at lead age 2-3 minutes, pre-empting the 60s call breathing room.
The AI-read daily cap is read then acted on, so two instances in a deploy can overshoot by one tick budget, and stores ignore rowCount.
Invoice void predicates were not atomic and a re-void was not idempotent, so a void racing a payment could leave the invoice inconsistent (codex I4).
Lead-call cap-trip alerts were not deduplicated (fixed with a min-id dedupe).

Lock-order inversion: the lab takes drink_plans then proposals while applyLineItemCancel takes proposals then drink_plans, so a client lab save during an admin cancel of a lab-owned add-on can deadlock and the admin sees a 500.

Unsigned-proposal drip enrollment was keyed per proposal, so two open proposals for one client and event date each ran the six-touch drip; 10 clients hit it June to September and 5 got every touch twice (prod 860 duplicates suppressed).

drip_stopped_at is checked only at enrollment and hand-off, never at send, so a touch in processing when Stop commits can come back through the cooldown defer, releaseClaim or the stranded-claim reaper, and a racing archive hand-off can insert fresh touches after 'Follow-ups stopped'.
The replacement payment-failed throttle claim (INSERT ... WHERE NOT EXISTS) had no unique index behind it, so two concurrent retries could still both claim and send

The lane draft treated failed payment rows as dead although Stripe lets a bounced debit be retried on the same intent, so a new payment could start beside a revivable one (D9: failed rows are live intents).

The check-then-create race on the checkout rails (in-flight check, then intent creation) is narrowed but not closed, so two near-simultaneous bank-debit payments can still both start (accepted residual).
refreshDisplayName does an unlocked SELECT-then-UPDATE, so two concurrent name saves for the same user can persist a stale display_name (accepted; the next save heals).

A pending refund row orphaned by a crash before the Stripe call could never be webhook-adopted, blocked refund headroom forever (permanent under-refund) and was hidden from refund history, with no healer.

The by-id refund-row adoption lookup checks only id, status and stripe_refund_id IS NULL and dropped the corroborating proposal_id, intent and amount predicates, so a caller passing a wrong id would reconcile against the wrong proposal.

Design stage: two concurrent overpayment-refund submits could both spend the same excess and drop amount_paid below total_price (demoting status, disarming autopay); the cap is now asserted under the proposals row lock.

Message dispatcher ticks could overlap (setInterval, no in-flight guard), so an overrunning run let the next tick re-select rows already sent but not yet marked and send duplicate balance reminders or autopay receipts
Critical dead-letter re-resolve treated a suppression group as dead while a sibling row was 'deferred' (a live retry in flight), so it could enqueue a duplicate critical message
The dispatcher's suppression key and reaper can double-send in a multi-instance deployment (unreachable with prod's single scheduler).
closeExtension lacked a fixed lock order (proposals first, then service_extensions) and could deadlock against settle.
The 60-second extension sweep had no reentrancy guard, so a slow tick could overlap the next.
A payment committing between the sweep's pre-read and its invoice void leaves an 'expired' extension with a PAID invoice that no heal path revisits; only a TOCTOU detector alert covers it.
Concurrent Twilio retries that raced past the inbound SELECT-dedup hit the new unique twilio_sid index as a 23505 and returned 500 instead of a graceful duplicate no-op
The press-1 escalation cap was only advisory under concurrency (12 legs through a cap of 3) until claimEscalationUnderCap hard-bounded it.
The sms_optouts boot backfill runs on the incoming instance, so a STOP the outgoing instance handles mid-deploy writes the preference but no sms_optouts row until the next boot (via 4430906a).
Re-arming the Thumbtack harvest before merging a duplicate client re-collided and created a double event on 7/18.
The agent could send a first reply twice on a retry until a three-layer guard (pre-click journal, post-click catch, report retries) was added (agent blocker).
The already_replied guard used an instant isVisible after the settle race, so a CTA painting before Quick Reply on an answered mid-hydration thread could read as pristine and double-send
With no back-off when a composer was already present, the agent raced manual replies and double-sent six confirmed times
A clickedSend skew path remains in the agent (residual low; detail not recorded).

The dev DB silently lacked shifts_status_check, which prod always carried, because its EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS DO-block ADD failed on every boot against three legacy status='confirmed' rows while initDb printed success, so dev accepted shift writes prod rejects until 610ef433 healed it.

Schema DO blocks wrapped in EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN NULL swallowed constraint failures, and dedupe-index CREATE failures (23505) were swallowed as idempotent, so narrowed or absent constraints and indexes booted green.

CONSTRAINT_CONTRACT covered 2 of the 20 bare DROP+ADD constraint pairs it exists for, omitting users_role_check (auth), service_addons_applies_to_check and message_log_status_check, and its pg_constraint lookup was not scoped by table, so a same-named constraint on another table could satisfy a contract (all closed in 49d6f919; email_sends_recipient_check is the separate open cluster).

email_sends_recipient_check (the lead_id/client_id XOR) is re-added by a bare DROP-then-ADD on every boot but stays outside CONSTRAINT_CONTRACT because the manifest has no presence-only entry kind, so its absence would go unreported (member f3-78 is the aggregate of all 20 bare DROP-then-ADD pairs, which ranks this one and three tip FKs highest).

CONSTRAINT_CONTRACT's mustContain literal match can false-pass on a multi-arm CHECK whose quoted value sits in an arm about a different column (latent: every contracted constraint is single-column today).
thumbtack_leads.event_duration was INTEGER, so a fractional duration (a 6:00-9:30 window) threw 22P02 in the webhook transaction, 500'd and dropped the lead while Thumbtack retries kept failing.

proposals_archive_reason_check was defined twice with different lists (the first missing option_not_chosen), so an initDb interrupted between them left the narrow one and every option_not_chosen archive failed 23514; flagged on 2026-07-01, it hit dev on 2026-08-14 while prod was one incomplete boot away.

invoice_payments had no unique constraint on (invoice_id, payment_id), so one payment could be linked to one invoice twice as positive links (closed with the partial unique uq_invoice_payments_positive_link WHERE amount > 0, audit F7).

message_log.client_id was NOT NULL with NO ACTION, the only client FK without ON DELETE SET NULL, contradicting the invariant clientMerge.js documents, so client merge and cleanup survived only by statement ordering (member m2-96 is the P0 schema-hygiene aggregate that also covered unvalidated CHECKs, dead columns, non-timestamptz timestamps and a missing index).

The Enhancement Lab invoice find-or-create has no backing unique index (invoices(proposal_id) WHERE label='Enhancement Lab' AND status IN ('sent','partially_paid')), so only the plan-row FOR UPDATE stands between concurrent saves and a duplicate Lab invoice.
The proposal_refunds_total_scope_check DO block matches pg_constraint on conname alone rather than (conrelid, conname), so a same-named constraint on another table would be mistaken for it.

idx_email_leads_email is UNIQUE on raw email rather than LOWER(email), so case-variant lead rows coexist and the cannot-resurrect-an-unsubscribed-lead guard that capture-lead and smsOptIn rely on is defeated by any uppercase-stored row.

All eight FOREIGN KEY statements, plus a stray ALTER TABLE proposal_addons ADD COLUMN that had drifted into the block, shared one DO block whose EXCEPTION handler only RAISE NOTICEs, so one failure rolled back the whole block, left a fresh DB on NO ACTION and never reached initDb's unexpected array.

thumbtack_leads.created_at was nullable while five predicates (the first-reply offer query and the sweep's retirement arm) assume it is set, so a NULL row would sit pending forever, invisible to both.

scheduled_messages_status_check was defined three times and the earlier definitions lacked processing, dead_letter and suppressed_by_sibling, so every boot opened a window where dispatcher claims raised 23514 and the generic catch marked them terminally failed, dropping due messages (the same e7e12c7a sweep aligned the earlier definitions of scheduled_messages_channel_check, users_onboarding_status_check and drink_plans_proposal_id_fkey).

idx_sms_messages_twilio_sid and idx_scheduled_messages_pending_uniq were dropped and recreated by a bare DROP-then-CREATE on every boot with no wrapping transaction, so the inbound SMS and scheduled-message enqueue dedupe guards were absent during each deploy (e7e12c7a only added them to CRITICAL_INDEXES; 81148d8b removed the per-boot drop).
The email_leads upsert's COALESCE(email_leads.name, EXCLUDED.name) is dead because name is NOT NULL, so an 'Unknown' name from capture-lead is never upgraded to the real one.

No CHECK prevents an approved, undropped shift_requests row with a NULL position, so such a row would be silently undercounted and dropped from the payrollAccrual tip split, and approved_by_role (which filters position IS NOT NULL) and approved_count agree only by convention across five write paths.
staff_reviews has no confirmed_at column, so the confirm that makes a review bounty owed leaves no timestamp and when a bounty became owed cannot be reconstructed from the table.
Missed and after-hours lead-call chains raised attention-feed items and lead_call emails as if they were faults although nothing could be done; the owner ruled that only system faults should alert.

The 2026-06-22 npm audit reported 11 vulnerabilities, 2 high (qs via express, undici, form-data, dompurify), cleared in 7804a16b by express 4.22.2, dompurify 3.4.11 and undici/form-data overrides (the uuid advisory member c2-327 names was deferred there, not fixed).

tips and tip_page_feedback user FKs were created without ON DELETE (NO ACTION); reviewed_by blocked deleting a reviewing admin instead of nulling

schema.sql is not auto-applied to the dev DB, so dev drifts until ALTERs are hand-applied.

The pre-existing /lead-cost lookup on thumbtack_leads.proposal_id had no index.

The specialty-liqueurs gated UPDATE's WHERE literal did not match the true historical seed text, so the guard would not fire on un-migrated DBs (inert on prod).
schema.sql defines the proposals.status CHECK three times and only the last is canonical.

The cancel-flow spec's archive_reason 'drb_cancelled' would have violated the existing CHECK.
message_log's status CHECK allowed only sent and failed, so bounce writes would fail 23514.
Extension money columns lacked a non-negative CHECK.

The shifts out_of_area_* ADD COLUMNs came after the cap-check DO block, so on a first prod boot the CHECK referenced a column that did not exist yet (42703) and the constraint was silently absent for that boot

Prod's soft-drink-addon description was hand-edited to a third text matching neither schema.sql's guard nor its replacement, so the guarded UPDATE could never fire again and a fresh database would seed different client-facing copy than prod.
schema.sql drops and re-adds the email_sends CHECK on every boot, taking an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock and a validation scan per deploy instead of using a guarded DO block.
The soft-drink-addon convergence IN() list missed the em-dash-era description variant seeded roughly Apr 22 to Jul 11, so restoring a snapshot from that window would resurrect stale copy.
idx_clients_email_unique is unique on the raw email, so case and whitespace variants of one address can exist as separate client rows (every matcher must lower(btrim())).

Five unnamed inline CHECKs inside CREATE TABLE diverged from the later ADD CONSTRAINT of the same auto-generated name (including the money proposal_payments_payment_type_check and the auth users_role_check), and the static guard could not read the inline form (fresh-DB blast radius)

proposals_gratuity_jar_check's earlier definition lacks the floor-rate arm, so during a partial boot a mandated no-jar proposal at or above its floor but under $50 per staff-hour would be rejected (the 2026-08-14 definitive sweep ruled it not a trap: the earlier site is IF NOT EXISTS and a NOT LIKE guard swaps in the full body, so a fresh boot self-heals).
The new per-FK guards first matched on constraint name without a conrelid pin, so a guard could match another table's constraint; three agents flagged it.

The boot-time staleness checks for idx_sms_messages_twilio_sid and idx_scheduled_messages_pending_uniq matched name, uniqueness and predicate only, so a same-named index on another table or column set, or an invalid index left by a failed CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, passed as healthy; the DROP INDEX was also not schema-qualified

idx_invoices_invoice_number is a plain non-unique index on dev because CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS matched the existing name, so invoice-number uniqueness never applied and nothing alerts (prod unverified)

The requires_provisioning seed missed the 3 BYOB bundles and 7 class_supplies add-ons, so bundle-only events got no Supplies chip, no shift transport requirement and no $20 equipment_supplies duty (found on a 10/03 event; shifts 396, 397, 379, 399 backfilled).
sms_optouts.source's CHECK lives only inside CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, so a new source value never reaches an existing table (via 4430906a).
message_log.sent_by is ON DELETE SET NULL, so deleting an admin users row turns their attributed sends into automated ones in contact history and Inbox.
inbox_reads has no index on updated_at or status, so the stats query and the stale-pending sweep scan it every minute and on every GET /inbox.
proposals_source_check is add-if-missing, so widening it for a new source (zola) needs a new drop-and-re-add block or prod keeps the old CHECK (the spec fleet's shared blocker).
seedTestData.js:365 and :425 inserted shifts with a status the constraint forbids, which is what created the legacy dev rows that blocked adding shifts_status_check on dev for months
Badge-counts selected applications.onboarding_status, a column that lives on users, so the query errored
Badge-count query called json_array_length on positions_needed without checking the JSON type, so a scalar value made the query error
Hiring applications list and detail read onboarding step flags from users, but those columns live on onboarding_progress
Stub-to-real user link Step 2 reassigned shift_requests without checking for a both-non-approved pair on the same shift, so it crashed on UNIQUE(shift_id, user_id)

An idle seniority save rewrote the row and the contractor_profiles BEFORE UPDATE trigger restamped updated_at, re-aiming which staffer a STOP on a shared inbound number lands on (smsInbound orders by updated_at)
Client email was stored with its case preserved, so case-variant duplicate client records slipped past the unique check.
VALID_SOURCES lacked 'checkcherry' after the clients_source_check extension, so every imported client's admin edit would 400 (a missed mirror in the 5-way source sync).
Consult and shopping-list-source routes used FOR UPDATE on a query that LEFT JOINs proposals; Postgres rejects locking the nullable side, so 'Generate shopping list' returned a generic 500
Admin drink-plan status PATCH allowlist lacked 'exploration_saved', which the DB constraint allows, so admins could not set it
VALID_LEAD_SOURCES omitted quote_wizard and potion_lab, drifting from the email_leads lead_source CHECK and the client lists

PUT /progress/step used $1 in untyped CASE WHEN text comparisons and as the varchar last_completed_step, the parameter-type pattern behind DRBARTENDER-SERVER-G (preventive; this SQL had shipped since March with no recorded failure)

The cancel-time clawback capture compared shift position without LOWER(TRIM()), so a padded legacy or hand-edited position would be missed (unreachable in practice because the shift_requests CHECK blocks padded rows).

Both cancel-line suites seeded shifts with status='confirmed', which shifts_status_check rejects; they passed locally only because the dev DB lacks the CHECK, and failed on the prod-shaped ci-smoke branch.

Proposal status PATCH used $1 both as the varchar status and in untyped CASE WHEN comparisons, so Postgres deduced inconsistent types and status changes returned 500 (Sentry DRBARTENDER-SERVER-G; introduced by fd6d0767)
Proposal DELETE left its scheduled_messages behind because scheduled_messages.entity_id has no FK to cascade
Admin proposal create blind-inserted the client, so an email that already existed hit idx_clients_email_unique (23505, Sentry DRBARTENDER-SERVER-J) instead of reusing the client
Public lead capture inserted any client-supplied lead_source, so a value outside the email_leads CHECK set made the INSERT fail with 500
shifts.js and calendar.js referenced dead first_name/last_name columns
Shift writes did not maintain updated_at.
The first barRequiredSql draft used bare num_bars > 0, but num_bars DEFAULTs to 1 and 17 prod proposals carry a defaulted bar with no bar money, an over-claim that four bare-request tests caught.
Staff payouts list returned event_count from an uncast COUNT(*), so node-pg delivered a bigint string instead of a number (pg type contract between DB and code)
Payment-link INSERT's ON CONFLICT target omitted the partial-index predicate, so Postgres could not infer idx_stripe_sessions_payment_link and the insert errored
refreshDisplayNames restamped updated_at on every row through the BEFORE UPDATE trigger, re-arming shared-number STOP attribution
applySeniorityBackfill's unguarded UPDATE restamped updated_at on every written row and on re-runs, re-arming shared-number STOP attribution
autoAssign seat counting compared position without LOWER(TRIM()), so a padded legacy position would be miscounted.
coverBroadcast role bucketing compared position without LOWER(TRIM()), so a padded legacy position would be mis-bucketed.

eventCreation.js hardcodes STAFFING_ADDON_MIN_HOURS = 4 to recover banquet-server and barback headcount, correct only while those service_addons rows read minimum_hours 4.0, so a catalog change silently mis-counts headcount and shifts.
Labrat purge deleted proposals and payments without first deleting proposal_refunds, which reference both with ON DELETE RESTRICT, so the purge would abort if a test proposal had a refund
Labrat purge deleted proposals while invoices still referenced them (invoices.proposal_id ON DELETE RESTRICT), so the purge failed on invoices_proposal_id_fkey (Sentry DRBARTENDER-SERVER-K)

appendRefundLine appends a Refund adjustment line without checking validateAdjustments' line-count cap, so a booking already at the cap ends one line over and every later editor save is refused until a line is removed.

Dispatcher lookupEntity for shifts selected shifts.archived_at, a column that never existed (added by 6e6a7b38 the day before), so shift-entity scheduled message lookups would error; the subject calls it an unused column
Dev-mode sendSMS returned the constant sid 'dev-skipped', which collided on the partial-unique twilio_sid index so the second logged dev send failed

Acknowledged Stripe payout lines are permanently excluded from re-matching and the unmatched count, and the acknowledged_at backfill UPDATE replays on every boot, so hand-clearing acknowledged_at is re-stamped at the next deploy and a later-matchable line is never re-matched (manual matchLine has no UI).
The client axios was on a range with a prototype-pollution advisory on the JWT-bearing fetcher; no taxonomy key covers vulnerable dependencies.
Dependencies carried known vulnerabilities (axios SSRF, fast-xml-parser, DOMPurify, brace-expansion) fixed by npm audit (vulnerable dependency; no key fits)
Dependency vulnerability (no taxonomy class): npm audit flagged vulnerable packages, fixed by npm audit fix without --force alongside a sharp 0.34 to 0.35 bump.

The sign_failed breadcrumb insert was awaited instead of fire-and-forget like the viewed insert, lacked the proxy-validated ip, and paged at warning for every refusal rather than only TOTAL_CHANGED (other: no taxonomy key for logging and alert levels)
Extension terms-acceptance stamps were not taking the proxy-validated req.ip as the client address (gate catch; acceptance-record integrity, no taxonomy key fits).

DELETE /shifts/requests/:id deletes a payroll-bearing roster row without logAdminAction, unlike the out-of-area PUT beside it, so no audit record of the removed money line exists (other: no taxonomy key covers missing audit logging).
Every successful passkey unlock was captured to Sentry as an info event, keeping a Sentry issue permanently open from routine use (other: no taxonomy key for alert noise)
Resend quota exhaustion was captured as a paging Sentry error instead of a warning breadcrumb (Sentry SERVER-Q/12) (other: a needless page or alert, not a swallowed error).

Reading a legacy pricing snapshot without _version fired captureMessage (85 events, the loudest server issue, burying real errors), throttled once per process so the context was rarely present when a real error landed (other: no taxonomy key for alert noise)

The Stripe payout sweep counted 119 pre-cutover payouts that can never match as stuck forever, firing a permanent Sentry alert with no acknowledgement path (Sentry SERVER-1G) (other: a needless page or alert, not a swallowed error).
The client payroll freeze gate did not match the server, which treats a processing period as frozen.
Approving past a role's capacity had no over-fill confirm guard.
The cancel-flow spec's open-invoice query omitted partially_paid invoices.
The client sign pad accepted without an explicit Accept-signature step, allowing an accidental acceptance.

ShiftDrawer's per-role fill math counted emergency-dropped staff (status approved with dropped_at set, returned unfiltered by GET /shifts/detail/:id) as filling their slot and showed them Confirmed, so the assign picker skipped the very role needing a replacement.

The desktop ShiftDrawer approves a cover claim through POST /shifts/:id/assign, which never runs approveAndCascade, so the original staffer stays approved with cover still requested; PUT /shifts/requests/:id, the only path that cascades, has no caller.
Hosted-package events were treated as owing a client shopping list: eventPlanState owed one, and they entered the admin prep queue and the List to review chip.
eventStatusChip read e.shift_status, a field the feed never emits, so a shift cancelled on its own kept chipping 'Paid in full'
markReviewed (Save & next, Cmd+Enter) did not re-check row problems, so a blocked drink could be marked reviewed, and it did not await an in-flight PUT.
Copy compare link was offered on every grouped proposal; with an option still in draft the public compare page skipped to the sign page, sending the client straight to a contract (group 20 in prod).
Admin Mark-accepted fired with no confirmation, allowing an accidental accept.
The admin client's canRecordPayment did not gate archived proposals (left as a UX follow-up).

Admin consumers re-derived 'upcoming' from the date alone, so cancelled events leaked into the Overview header count and the Needs-attention Staffing queue (upcoming 18 vs 16, need-staff 11 vs 9 in prod)
The PayrollStatus overdue detector ignored the new 'reopened' status, so the overdue dot would go dark for a reopened late period.
The proposal editor's reprice confirm gate missed completed proposals, so a save that reprices and bills a completed event server-side skipped the confirm modal.
Admin reactivate set onboarding_status 'submitted', a dead status the portal no longer routes, and the staff Onboarding tab filtered on dead statuses

A failed 3DS redirect lands on ?paid=true with redirect_status=failed, and the page showed 'Booking confirmed' for a payment that did not happen
paidState treated status 'completed' as paid, so an event an admin hand-set to completed with a balance still owed rendered as paid and lost its pay link
A settle refetch that came back unsettled was handed to the page as paid instead of landing in the fallback state
The client portal's next-up widget offered 'Review & book' for an archived proposal, linking to /proposal/:token, which 404s once archived
The portal Prescription tab rendered Review & book, the Pay balance fallback and a share link, all pointing at the 404ing /proposal/:token of an archived proposal
As planned, the edit sheet multi-shift note counted cancelled shifts.

As planned, an approval with no role on file did not fill a slot, so the phone would offer a filled slot again (none in prod).
The staff-portal landing treated only 'hired' as go-onboard, so an applicant moved to in_progress by the Hire button was stranded on 'Application Received, sit tight'.
Logout purged the phone's enrolled flag while the server credential and OS passkey survived, so the next enrollment threw InvalidStateError forever.
Two inactive client-request duplicate cocktail rows with empty ingredient lists sat in prod, one flagged 'reviewed' while empty, so a recipe could carry the reviewed flag with no build
Plan 2d cancelled pending drip touches only on archive, so drip emails would keep sending after the client signed and paid

The staff-hub spec's Reviews card lacked the state 'confirmed, bounty waiting for an open period'.
The out-of-area lock was not released on the six roster-removal paths, including the ShiftDrawer DELETE.
Held payroll extras were tracked by a fragile note marker, replaced by a structural payout_events.held_state.
Pay period Jun 2-8 is empty after its only payout (the owner's) was deleted, and it sits open forever.

At least one live send path moves a proposal to viewed without stamping sent_at (3 of the 29 null rows, ids 628, 681 and 764, were created in Aug 2026), so the Money Board gap re-accrues after any backfill.
The quote wizard posts sms_consent:false for an un-ticked box, stamping a hard sms_opt_out_at that blocks the number from every future opt-in until they text START.
Seed and import scripts write event duration without the venue-curfew guard.
Reverting an applicant's status to 'applied' re-sent the 'we received your application' email
Admin application status changes (interview, hired, rejected) sent applicants no email, so they were never told their status moved (issue #19)
Reject endpoint accepted an applicant who was already rejected
Payout edits were blocked only for paid periods, not processing ones, while mark-paid copies stored totals (L3).

Payroll had no way to exempt the owner, who takes no draw, so his worked shifts created payouts that were deleted by hand (payouts 63 and 70) or sat pending forever, leaving pay period 72 unable to close on him alone and the pending queue growing unbounded.
The payroll redesign spec reopened a period back to 'open', which every accrual, clawback and late-tip writer accepts; redesigned as a new 'reopened' status those writers refuse.
Processing a pay period early would freeze its lines before all shifts accrued, a wage blackhole (force guard added).
toggle-draw would park a contractor whose takes_draw says they take a draw, since the flag was only a render gate, not server-side authority
Parking the last pending payout as no_draw finalized the pay period with no confirmation (a one-way door) until a confirm_finalize gate returning 409 was added.

Payroll Process runs listUnattributedDuties on a reopened pay period while accrual writes nothing into a non-open period, so a pre-2026-09-28 bundle event in a reopened period demands an equipment_supplies attribution (409 until given) and the attributed worker is then paid nothing.
Stale duty attributions blocked Process with a 409 even when nobody was eligible.

The staff-hub summary counts and the active-staff roster feed hand-write the same status predicate separately with no shared helper or test, and reviewed or submitted rows land in the feed but in none of the four counts, so the counts can silently stop summing to the table.
The admin onboarding-status change route's validStatuses list omits 'suspended' while other surfaces know it, so an admin cannot set a staffer to suspended there.

40 staff accounts in hired or in_progress with no applications row appear on no admin list (the Hiring feed INNER JOINs applications and GET /admin/active-staff selects only approved, reviewed, submitted and deactivated), so nobody can clear or deactivate them from a list screen.
A pre-hire who already had an account hit the application gate and could only get through via the admin Hire button.
Late Cal.com cancel and no-show webhooks overwrote a consult an admin had already marked completed
Staff calendar feed, team lists and the staff event history query (USER_EVENTS_SQL) still included shifts the staffer had emergency-dropped
The portal focus picker ordered by date only, so a newer draft on the same date shadowed a booked proposal (proposal 626 shown instead of the booking).
GET /api/client-portal/proposals/:token has no status filter, so archived proposals are only unlisted, not unreachable, in the client portal.

Now that a repeat Thumbtack lead lands on the existing client, each repeat adds an unreviewed auto-draft proposal that a client with a portal login sees, price snapshot included, on the portal focus card before any admin has reviewed or sent it.
Typing an email straight into the admin client editor never flips email_harvest_status from pending (15 pending-with-email rows on 2026-09-10).

PUT /clients/:id updates the email but never resets email_status 'bad' and the one reset route has no client caller, so after an admin fixes a bounced address every immediate and scheduled email to that client is still dropped as bad_contact.
The request-alias collision check counted recipe-less draft rows, so an admin who closed an empty Add-recipe drawer was dead-ended by a 409 on the very duplicate the action prevents (round-1 MEDIUM).
Send-modal SMS channel availability lacked the hosted and token guards the email channel had.
labState returned ready instead of not_ready for a pre-deposit proposal (no pre-booking gate, unlike GET /t/:token), so a public drink-plan token could fold add-ons into an unsigned contract.
The Lab GET serves the full shelf payload even when the plan is not_ready or locked; only the client gates rendering.
labListRefresh stage UPDATE is the one drink_plans writer with no finalize guard, reachable from the lab PUT deferred refresh and from cancelLineItem.js, which has no finalize check at all.
Post-approve edits reverted an approved shopping list to pending_review, so every link already in the client's inbox showed the pending screen (approved snapshot added).
Every edit to an approved shopping list hid it from the client, and the only way to re-show it re-approved and re-emailed, so a client on a live call got an email per edit.

The server-derived mocktail flip was enforced version-blind, billing undisclosed per-guest charges to legacy v1 plans and able to strip admin-seeded pair rows (now gated on planner_version >= 2 with package_items present).
The client submit path lacks a finalized_at guard.
Campaign DELETE archived unconditionally, including a campaign mid-send, so the run kept mailing, the release UPDATE matched nothing, and the campaign stranded archived with a claim-stamp sent_at.

The campaign archive guard refused any campaign in 'sending' with no staleness escape, so a process death mid-send left it unarchivable forever, while the send's own run claim treated the same stale claim as abandoned
POST /campaigns/:id/test mailed the campaign body to any address without an opt-out check.
A marketing spam complaint flipped clients.email_status to 'bad', which gates proposals, invoices and agreements, and nothing ever wrote it back, so one complaint killed a client's billing email.

Legacy proposal-less shifts hardcode approved_by_role: {} and cover_requested_at: null in the event-details payload, so a filled manual shift renders fully open ('Request this shift' instead of 'Join waitlist') and an active cover never shows its chip.
Invoices with payments applied could be voided

Onboarding payment submit forced tip_page_active = TRUE, re-activating a tip page an admin had deactivated
PUT /progress/step accepted writes after onboarding was complete, so a bounced client regressed last_completed_step on a finished account
Proposal status PATCH allowed any status jump (e.g. completed back to draft) with no state machine

The new proposal resend emailed archived and paid proposals until constrained to sent, viewed, modified and accepted.

record-payment rejects confirmed proposals, so a check or cash balance cannot be recorded through the UI (accepted; manual UPDATE).

An unrelated edit on a paid proposal stamped gratuity origin 'staffing' when the rate had not changed.

Signing sets status accepted without suppressing pending drip rows and the drip handlers refuse only archived at send time, so a client who signs and abandons checkout keeps getting 'Did you get the proposal?' through touch 5.

The Stop follow-ups route keys on OPEN_STATUS_LIST (sent, viewed, modified), so on an accepted proposal the button is hidden, a direct POST answers 409 DRIP_NOT_ACTIVE, and an accepted sibling is left out of the whole-event stop.

DATE columns (event date, invoice due date, balance due date) were rendered with local-time toLocaleDateString and computed with local setDate, showing a day early in US browsers
The phone events list date rail (railParts in eventCards.js) shows no year, so a 2027 event reads out of order.
LabLedger rendered due dates without a local-noon anchor (shifting the day) and money without two decimals.
The client portal countdown parsed event_date as a timestamp and showed NaN.

The staff Pay screen sliced String(iso).slice(0,10) off the raw paid_at the API returns, so it showed the UTC day and disagreed with the corrected PDF and the Chicago-year 1099; still present at 4d674da4 despite the 8/20 sweep marking it fixed.
The TODAY rail uses the device day rather than a fixed business timezone (same as the desktop list).

The UTC-day toISOString().slice(0,10) shape sits at 34 sites across 28 non-test files (plus 13 test files), 14 of them classified dangerous, with the helper hand-rolled sixteen times.

The clawback and admin-payroll suites keyed current-period fixtures on UTC (CURRENT_DATE, toISOString) while the code uses chicagoTodayYmd, so they went red every Chicago evening after the UTC rollover.
The tips ledger cast a date-only 'to' bound to that day's midnight, so tipped_at <= to dropped every tip after 00:00 on the selected day and understated the ledger total.

The 1099 tax year used EXTRACT(YEAR FROM paid_at) in the GMT session, so a payout marked paid after 6pm Chicago on Dec 31 filed into the next tax year.

area: dev DB via Neon pooler (PgBouncer transaction mode)
what: A planning subagent created TEMP tables named clients, proposals and inbox_reads through the pooled dev URL; they outlived its session on a PgBouncer backend and shadowed the public tables for every other window (column phone does not exist).
An idle-in-transaction pg client error had no pool error handler and crashed the server process (Sentry SERVER-17).
The pg pool max of 20 was below one Money Board load (about 23 concurrent checkouts across dashboard-stats and financials), queueing requests toward the 10s connect timeout.

server/db/index.js sets no idleTimeoutMillis, so pg reaps idle clients after 10s and each page load dials 5 to 12 fresh Neon TLS connections at about 350-625ms each (five Sentry 'N+1 Query' groups including SERVER-11).

On 2026-10-08 two in-flight pg queries failed with read ECONNABORTED, so the Thumbtack agent's GET /api/admin/thumbtack/pending-first-replies?limit=3 poll got a 500 (4 events since 2026-07-28); the agent re-polls.

pool.on('error') in server/db/index.js captures every idle pg pool client the backend or network drops (read ECONNABORTED or ETIMEDOUT, 'Connection terminated unexpectedly') as a Sentry error though no request fails, pinned on whichever request was in scope (SERVER-1J, SERVER-2).
admin/payroll.js post-COMMIT refreshes used pool.query while still holding the request's client.
The no-draw engine's audit write deadlocked on a one-connection path (one-connection audit deadlock).
An auth.js registration path took a second pooled connection while holding its rolled-back client.
calcom.test.js never ended the pg pool in an after hook, leaving the test process holding open connections
coverageContext ran its queries concurrently on the held transaction client, which pg@9 rejects.
The menu-print proxy piped without stream.pipeline, so a client disconnect did not tear down the R2 stream

The campaign send used pg_try_advisory_lock as its mutex, a no-op on Neon's PgBouncer pooler (checkouts share one backend session, locks are re-entrant and one request can release another's), so concurrent sends were not excluded.
A plain FOR UPDATE on /cancel/refund would self-deadlock against refund reconciliation, so it needed an advisory transaction lock.
POST /:id/cancel-line/preview runs the whole cancel mutation then rolls back, so a nominally read-only preview holds exclusive row locks for the full core and burns SERIAL values.
Proposal POST and PATCH held the pooled client through the audit/email/drip/invoice tail, taking two connections per request

The quote-wizard capture-lead handler kept its pooled client while its post-commit abandoned-quote enrollment ran pool.query on a second connection, so a wizard spike could exhaust and deadlock the pool.
Stripe webhook and record-payment ran BEGIN/COMMIT through pool.query on whatever connection was free, so their transactions had no isolation

The Thumbtack /leads webhook held its pooled client until the finally block while the post-commit tail's createDraftProposalFromLead opened its own pool connection and transaction, using two connections per webhook that retries could burst.
applyPackageLineup2026 ran its transaction through pool.query instead of one dedicated client.
Invoice void code made Stripe API calls while holding a pooled DB connection.
applyLineItemCancel locks proposals then drink_plans while drinkPlans/lab.js locks drink_plans then proposals, so concurrent runs can deadlock and Postgres aborts one with a 500.

scheduleMessage ran its INSERT on the bare pool while PATCH /proposals/:id held a transaction, so re-rescheduling an event with drink-plan nudge rows self-deadlocked holding the proposal row lock (reproduced live).
payrollClawback wrote its deferral marker on a fresh pooled connection while holding one, risking pool exhaustion in a refund or dispute webhook storm.
payrollLateTip wrote its deferral marker on a fresh pooled connection while holding one.
Reschedule's insertIfMissing delegated to scheduleMessage, which inserted on the module pool, so long-lead reminder rows escaped rescheduleProposalInTx's transaction and survived a rollback
dispatchPushRow held a DB transaction open across web-push sends, an idle-in-transaction FATAL that crashed the server (Sentry SERVER-17).
The escalation path's DB connect plus lock wait can take about 13s against Twilio's 15s webhook ceiling.
Plan 2d would have run the new dispatcher's nurture touches alongside the legacy email-sequence engine's Abandoned Quote Followup, double-sending to the same clients
The planner v2 plan put one-time lineup data UPDATEs in the boot path, where they would re-run on every boot (moved to a one-time script).
The payroll orphan sweep silently deleted positive adjustments instead of preserving them.
Scheduler tick staggers outlast Render's deploy drain only by timing luck, not design, so an overlapping deploy could double-run a tick.
cc-balance-invoice.js --only with a malformed value parsed to NaN, which is falsy, so the id filter vanished and --apply would mint every eligible proposal instead of the one asked for.

Every web instance started every scheduler (balance/autopay, event-completion, auto-assign, email-sequence, quote-draft-cleanup), so N instances would run each job, autopay charges and emails included, N times; stopgapped by the RUN_SCHEDULERS env guard (false on extra instances), dedicated worker deferred.
With schedulers globally disabled (RUN_SCHEDULERS=false or a non-prod boot) the boot path still ran clearHealthRow for each scheduler, wiping the primary instance's heartbeat rows in the shared DB
Schedulers booted by default under any NODE_ENV, so a dev server iterated the shared DB's scheduled_messages and sent real Resend and Twilio messages, burning provider allotments
Turning TT_AUTOREPLY_ENABLED on retro-enqueues leads younger than 1h (Arm B(2) residual), so a flip could auto-reply to leads already being worked.
Autopay-failure throttle marked 'the latest autopay_failed row' as notified, which could be a stale older row if the new INSERT failed, so the admin was re-emailed every cycle
Autopay scheduler emailed the admin on every hourly failure for a permanently dead card, with no throttle

The first consult dial cap summed admin_ring over consult_call_attempts rows, but the R16 reschedule clear deletes skipped rows, so ring, reschedule away and reschedule back erased billed rings from the window (measured 3 to 0) and the ceiling never engaged; caps now count the append-only call_audit ledger

The consult chain cap counted only non-skipped chains (ruling R15), so booking a public Cal.com slot, letting it ring, cancelling and rebooking cost up to three billed US legs per cycle with nothing bounding the dialing, while a code comment claimed the cap bounded sustained spend
The unresolved-reschedule email's rolling throttle window was defeatable because each stop reopened it.
A client with several unsigned proposals for one event got a drip sequence per proposal instead of one per client per event.
The drip archive hand-off can resurrect a failed touch (medium pushed as-is).
The first-reply sweep's Arm A preempted the call delay, so a reply confirmed 2-3 minutes after arrival got its call seconds later, the too-fast ring the delay exists to prevent
As sketched, a partial Gmail page left the cursor in place, so the next tick re-listed and re-fetched the same oldest ids against the per-tick cap and never got past them.
With the AI read on, the idle 60-second tick recomputes the inbox about every third minute, about 0.25 to 0.5 GB a day of Neon transfer (owner decision pending).
Deleting pending scheduled rows is never a durable suppression, because any proposal PATCH re-enqueues pre-event rungs via schedulePreEventReminders.

The planned stale-refund sweeper would have listed Stripe refunds account-wide for rows with a NULL payment intent (stripe-node drops the undefined filter), letting its unique-amount fallback adopt another proposal's refund and corrupt the ledger.
The new full-drain dispatcher loop had no pass cap, so a row whose terminal-status write kept failing would be re-selected and re-dispatched without end inside one tick

Removing the labrat_purge scheduler also removed its clearHealthRow call (which only ran on the env-disabled branch), leaving an orphaned scheduler_health row that fired 'Scheduler stale: labrat_purge' every 15 minutes (SERVER-1M).
Fire-and-forget venue geocodes queued behind one 1 req/sec chain with no shedding, so a burst of shift creates stacked lookups a second apart into the future
The stranded-paid extension alert stormed urgent email and SMS every 60 seconds until a 24h per-extension throttle was added.
The extension sweep scheduler booted in step with the other schedulers until a 25s stagger was added.
The shift closure sweep is a single UPDATE, so one row with a bogus IANA event_timezone aborts the whole statement and no shift closes on any tick thereafter, rather than only the bad row failing.
The voicemail delivery sweep starved behind undeliverable lines (head-of-line) until the deliverable-line filter moved into SQL (line = ANY).
The 30-day ledger prune orphans primary-line voicemail audio that stays retained in Twilio (documented known 1a gap until R2).
webhook_events prune ran one unbounded DELETE, so after a long pause or on first run it could lock every expired row at once
The harvester's daily cap counted successful harvests instead of page opens, so failed opens never counted against the cap.
The 2026-07-11 payment and auth audit report was never persisted to the repo, so its three low/info findings were lost and the rest had to be reconstructed from session memory on 2026-07-13.

Agent files added to .claude/agents mid-session are not dispatchable until a restart because the registry is locked at session start, so freshly written review agents (the new design-stage fleet) failed with Agent type not found.

The agent registry is scoped to the launch CWD, so a session started from the home directory never loads os/.claude/agents and spec or lens fleet dispatches fail with Agent type not found until resent as general-purpose agents with the agent brief inlined.
Per-developer .claude/settings.local.json (local paths, permission allowlist) was tracked in the public repo
.gitignore did not exclude .env.* variants, *.key or *.pem, so secrets could be committed to the public repo
Husky pre-commit hook had no shebang and failed on Windows
The pre-commit 1000-line cap fired on stripeWebhook.js at merge and forced a --no-verify bypass until the webhook handlers were extracted.

The pre-push gates run against the shared checkout (diff origin/main..HEAD and the working tree) rather than the pushed refspec, so other batches' unpushed commits or another session's uncommitted files can fail a literal-sha push of unrelated commits.

The no-draw UI lane carried an orphaned reference that would fail the CI build (CI-orphan), fixed before merge (build break; no taxonomy class fits).
The grep binary crashed mid-session and, inside a 'grep || echo none' idiom, printed 'none', a false negative in an audit sweep (re-run through python)
Open defects such as the PUT /shifts/:id status hole were carried only in session handoffs or ARCHITECTURE.md, not the fix list, so they could be lost at a session boundary.
Big nested StructuredOutput schemas crashed the Fable synthesis agent at its retry cap, so the audit's findings had to be harvested from the workflow journal.

A session called the harvester a backstop by misreading email_harvest_attempts=0 (which counts only failed retries) as scraper-skipped, when the scraper is the primary email source (82% of harvested leads).

area: Claude Bash tool (shared cwd across parallel calls)

A foreground Bash call past 600s is backgrounded and dies with the session, so a hung gemini review wrote 0 bytes when the session ended.

what: The Bash tool decodes \uXXXX escapes in command text before bash sees them, so a U+2028 escape in a heredoc became a real line separator and broke a regex literal.

A session concluded from two live leads that a Thumbtack-native auto-reply was on and framed SERVER-1S as a reply-owner choice, but no native auto-reply exists; the fast replies were manual.

Parallel sessions share one git index in the os checkout, so a bare git commit sweeps in whatever another window has staged (5 paystub files on 2026-06-05, staged deletions in 23506f8 on 2026-07-10, and staged deletions riding be555426 on 2026-08-14), misattributing changes in history.

Review helper script set NODE_PATH with a non-raw Windows path string whose backslashes JavaScript drops as escapes, producing a wrong path
The PII denylist regexes in board-write.sh are not word-anchored, so snake_case identifiers containing in_, re_, ch_ or pi_ are rejected as Stripe ids.
board-write.sh appends without a blank line before the following ## heading (cosmetic).
board-write.sh did a plain git push of main after committing the board line, so a board write right after a lane merge nearly deployed 49 unpushed commits with no push cue and no push-time review
The CC transfer script did not register the dispatcher handler registry (only server boot wires it), found in dev integration including --resume recovery.
docs-drift pre-commit hook warned on every modification of a structural file, not only on added, removed or renamed files (false positives)
guard-os-main.sh blocks lane commits touching docs/superpowers specs or plans, so plan corrections found during a build and merges of main into a lane cannot be committed from the lane.
fixed_ref: open (workaround: commit on main, rebase lanes)

what: merge-lane.sh treats a foreign untracked plan doc left by another window as a dirty tree and refuses to merge.
scripts/mobile-capture.js hardcodes port 3000, so npm run mobile:check works only when the lane client itself runs on port 3000.
testdb-smoke.js fails on a listed suite file that is missing, but nothing notices a line quietly deleted from scripts/money-smoke-list.txt, so a money suite can drop out of the push gate silently.
stripePayoutSync.js was on the sensitive list but neither payout suite was on the money smoke gate, so the fail-closed Stripe payout guard had no push-time enforcement.
scripts/money-smoke-list.txt carries shifts.bonus.test.js but not its sibling shifts.removeReaccrue.test.js, so the push gate never runs the Remove re-accrual test.
The new contrast script treated a linear-gradient background as transparent and measured the page behind it, falsely reporting the avatar initials at 1.05:1
pushedShaFromStdin collapsed empty or unreadable pre-push stdin into 'nothing to push', which would have silently skipped every gate on every push
The gate receipt fingerprint used git status --porcelain (path and status letter, not bytes), so re-editing an already-dirty file kept a stale receipt valid
Unreadable stdin fell back to gating HEAD without invalidating the receipt, so a valid HEAD receipt was honored without confirming what ships
Unreadable stdin invalidated the receipt but then gated HEAD and exited 0, so a different pushed commit could ship ungated
The pidfile gate lock leaked on every signal, so Ctrl-C made 'stale lock present' routine, and a reused pid could wedge every future push while the message offered --no-verify

The gate's run-mode summary can print 'gate PASSED, skips the hook' right after 'no receipt was written' when the tree moved mid-run, because it re-reads the stale receipt (the hook still refuses it).
flock -n uses exit 1 for lock-held, so a gate that legitimately fails with exit 1 also prints 'another push gate is already running' after its real diagnostic.

No gate runs the non-money server suites or checks that a DB-touching *.test.js loads dotenv (npm test is not a gate and the push gate runs only the money smoke list and the client build), so a suite dead since birth shows only as a lower pass count; nine suites stayed dead for weeks and the proposed CI grep was left unbuilt.

The *EmailTemplates.js and *Scheduler.js globs missed the base files server/utils/emailTemplates.js, scheduledMessageDispatcher.js and dispatcherDeadLetters.js, so changes to the base email template and the send dispatcher escaped the sensitive review fleet.

server/routes/drinkPlans/submit.js, a public token-gated writer of total_price and total_price_override, matched no sensitive-paths glob, so the change behind the $627 overbill scaled to a light review.

The comms registry (server/utils/comms/*.js, comms/actions/*.js, routes/comms.js), which drives every admin-initiated client email and SMS plus the invoice draft-to-sent flip, matched no sensitive-paths glob, so the invoiceSend balance defect scaled to a light review.

server/routes/payment.js, which grants onboarding_status 'approved', and the onboarding promotion helper matched no sensitive-paths glob, so the auth-perimeter fix closing the self-promotion hole scaled to a light review.

server/routes/invoices.js (void and comp, mark-paid, payment linking, label create and rename, reconcile_total) was missed by the server/utils/invoice*.js glob, which never crosses '/', so a total_price semantics change in it landed at a light review.
scripts/*.js is absent from sensitive-paths.txt, so money-writing scripts such as the gratuity reset never trigger the review fleet on their own.

server/utils/changeRequests.js, whose priceProposedState turns a client-chosen configuration into a price for change requests and the public options quote, and the new publicOptions endpoint matched no sensitive-paths glob.

server/utils/marketingAudience.js (the single home of the unsubscribe suppression conditions) and the send-channel helpers messageSuppression.js, channelFallback.js and notificationChannelResolver.js were unlisted, so the email_enabled removal that touched them would not have triggered the fleet.

server/routes/staffPortal.js was not on sensitive-paths.txt (its sibling staffPortal/payouts.js was), so the change that introduced the CURRENT_DATE pay-period bug never pulled a money review.

Piping testdb-smoke.js through tail or head replaces its exit code with the pager exit code, so a pre-push BLOCKED gate run reports success.

The money smoke gate cannot fail on a failed schema statement: initDb logs and Sentry-reports per-statement errors and resolves, so the child exits 0 and the gate passes while a constraint silently did not build.
.gitignore matched node_modules/ and client/node_modules/ with a trailing slash (directories only), so Linux lane symlinks left every worktree born dirty and broke worktree cleanup.

worktree:new did not link the root .env into a lane, so dotenv found nothing and every server test or node -e DB script there failed (ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:5432, or 'client password must be a string'), and a git push from a worktree ran the pre-push suites without .env, failing three Stripe suites with misleading errors.
The worktree helper linked the root .env but not client/.env, so fresh lanes baked an empty REACT_APP_API_URL and API calls 500'd in a way that read as a code bug
npm run worktree:rm prints 'Merge the branch, or re-run with --force' after successfully removing the worktree, which reads like a failed removal.

On Windows, worktree:rm hit folders locked by a running dev server after it had already unlinked the junctions and deregistered the worktree, so git worktree remove failed and left a half-removed lane to clean up by hand.
The search plan had no re-verification after review fix rounds or a rebase, did not commit its review sections before the merge, and lacked the post-merge server suite.
Gemini second opinion could not run on the Linux box because its auth was broken, so the SERVER-15 plan got codex review only.
The 7/25 triage asserted WILDLIGHT-6 rode the WILDLIGHT-1 pool-error fix and resolved it in Sentry without a fix of its own; it regressed on 8/02.
The 6/22 triage treated SERVER-11 as pool exhaustion and raised pg max from 10 to 20, but it kept firing; the 7/25 triage traced it to cold-pool reconnect bursts.

server/routes/admin/payrollTax.js was absent from scripts/sensitive-paths.txt, so a change to it scaled to a light review instead of the full fleet.

server/routes/calendar.js was absent from scripts/sensitive-paths.txt, so a change to it scaled to a light review instead of the full fleet.

payouts.paystub.test.js, the only direct paystub suite, was not on money-smoke-list.txt, so the push-time money gate never ran it.

The staff-import getArg rejected the --flag=value form that its own preflight message suggested.

server/utils/balanceInvoiceMonitor.js was absent from scripts/sensitive-paths.txt, so a change to it scaled to a light review instead of the full fleet.

server/utils/businessTime.js, home of the Chicago-day helpers every payroll date path depends on, is absent from scripts/sensitive-paths.txt, so a change to it scales to a light review instead of the full fleet.

server/utils/orientationData.js was absent from scripts/sensitive-paths.txt, so a change to it scaled to a light review instead of the full fleet.
server/utils/paystubData.js, which assembles a tax document's money content, is absent from scripts/sensitive-paths.txt, so a change to it scales to a light review instead of the full fleet.
